The family is intersecting, meaning that \(F\cap F'\ne\varnothing\) for all \(F,F'\in\mathcal F\). Its covering number is \(t\), where the covering number is the minimum cardinality of a set \(C\subseteq V\) meeting every member of \(\mathcal F\).

In addition, choose a partition \(\mathcal F=\mathcal F_1\sqcup\cdots\sqcup\mathcal F_t\) into nonempty subfamilies and pairwise disjoint nonempty sets \(X_1,\ldots,X_t\subseteq V\) such that \(X_i\subseteq F\) for every \(F\in\mathcal F_i\). Define
\[
b(t)=\min\sum_{i=1}^{t}\bigl(k-|X_i|\bigr),

With \(\log\) denoting the natural logarithm, determine the exact value of
\[
\lim_{\substack{t\to\infty\\t\in\mathbb Z}}\frac{\log b(t)}{\log t}.

import itertools,json,os

def check(t):
 k=2*t
 cores=[]; pos=0
 for i in range(t):
  d=t-1-i
  cores.append(tuple(range(pos,pos+k-d)));pos+=k-d
 classes=[]
 for i in range(t):
  cls=[]
  for petal in itertools.product(*cores[i+1:]):
   F=frozenset(cores[i]+petal)
   assert len(F)==k
   cls.append(F)
  classes.append(cls)
 fam=sum(classes,[])
 assert len(set(fam))==len(fam)
 assert all(F&G for x,F in enumerate(fam) for G in fam[x:])
 assert all(all(set(cores[i])<=F for F in classes[i]) for i in range(t))
 # Any smaller cover extends to t-1, so exhaustive checking this level suffices.
 for C in itertools.combinations(range(pos),t-1):
  S=set(C)
  assert any(not(S&F) for F in fam)
 C={c[0] for c in cores}
 assert all(C&F for F in fam)
 return dict(t=t,k=k,n=pos,m=len(fam),b=sum(k-len(c) for c in cores),tau=t,checked_noncovers=__import__('math').comb(pos,t-1))
results=[check(t) for t in range(2,5)]
os.makedirs('workspace',exist_ok=True)
with open('workspace/agent4_tournament_checks.json','w') as f:json.dump(results,f,indent=2)

"""Exact finite check of owner-labelled sunflower compression lemma."""
from itertools import combinations,product
import json

def tau(edges,vertices):
 for r in range(len(vertices)+1):
  for c in combinations(vertices,r):
   if all(set(c)&e for e in edges):return r

def check(t,core_size):
 # Regular cyclic tournament t odd, enough values to produce a sunflower.
 cores=[frozenset(range(i*core_size,(i+1)*core_size)) for i in range(t)]
 owner={v:i for i,X in enumerate(cores) for v in X}
 d=(t-1)//2
 groups=[]
 for i in range(t):
  targets=[j for j in range(t) if 1<=(j-i)%t<=d]
  groups.append([cores[i]|frozenset(p) for p in product(*(cores[j] for j in targets))])
 edges=[e for g in groups for e in g]
 assert all(a&b for a,b in combinations(edges,2))
 assert tau(edges,list(owner))==t
 i=0; petals=[e-cores[i] for e in groups[i]]
 augmented=[frozenset([('v',v) for v in p]+[('c',owner[v]) for v in p]) for p in petals]
 L=d+2
 found=0
 for inds in combinations(range(len(petals)),L):
  kernel=frozenset.intersection(*(augmented[q] for q in inds))
  if any((augmented[a]&augmented[b])!=kernel for a,b in combinations(inds,2)):continue
  K=frozenset(v for typ,v in kernel if typ=='v')
  labels=set(v for typ,v in kernel if typ=='c')-{owner[v] for v in K}
  assert len(K)+len(labels)<=d
  additions=[cores[i]|K|frozenset(p) for p in product(*(cores[j] for j in sorted(labels)))]
  assert all(a&b for a in additions for b in edges)
  assert all(a&b for a,b in combinations(additions,2))
  assert tau(edges+additions,list(owner))==t
  found+=1
 return {'t':t,'d':d,'core_size':core_size,'edges':len(edges),'sunflowers_checked':found}
results=[check(3,3)]
# t=5,d=2,core_size=4: pairwise checks and all covers up to4 on20 vertices manageable.
results.append(check(5,4))
assert all(r['sunflowers_checked']>0 for r in results)
with open('workspace/agent2_compression_checks.json','w') as f:json.dump(results,f,indent=2)
with open('workspace/agent2_compression_checks.py','w') as f:f.write(open('scratchpad.py').read())
print(json.dumps(results,indent=2))

from pathlib import Path
text=r'''Universal lower bound proved by agent_3 (also independently agents_2,4).
Write D=sum_i d_i, d_i=k-|X_i|. Every union of m chosen original classes has covering number exactly m: cover by core representatives; any smaller cover plus representatives for omitted classes would contradict tau(F)=t. Its petal-family union also has covering number at least m, because a petal cover is an original-family cover.
Take m>=t/2 classes with d_i<=d=2D/t. Choose a maximal rainbow disjoint collection of petals R_i, i in I, |I|=r. Their union U has size <=rd and covers all petals in unselected low-deficit classes; otherwise add an avoiding petal. Thus m-r<=tau(unselected petals)<=|U|<=rd, i.e. m<=r(d+1).
For each chosen class i choose original edge F_i=Xi union R_i. For i!=j, F_i cap F_j nonempty; Xi cap Xj=empty and R_i cap R_j=empty. So either R_i cap Xj nonempty or R_j cap Xi nonempty. Each chosen petal meets at most |R_i|<=d disjoint cores. Consequently binom(r,2)<=sum_i |R_i|<=rd, and r<=2d+1 for r>0. Hence t/2<=m<=(2d+1)(d+1).
For t>=4, assuming D<t^(3/2)/20 gives d<sqrt(t)/10, so RHS/t < 8/400+6/(20 sqrt(t))+1/t <= .42 < .5, a contradiction. Thus b(t)>=t^(3/2)/20 for t>=4. This only gives liminf >=3/2, NOT the asked exact answer.
'''
Path('workspace/agent3_lower_proof.txt').write_text(text)
print(text)

from pathlib import Path
code='''import itertools,json,time
from pathlib import Path
out=[]
for t in range(2,7):
 # Cyclic orientation, tie in even order resolved by numerical order.
 arcs={(i,j) for i in range(t) for j in range(t) if i!=j and ((j-i)%t<t/2 or ((j-i)%t==t/2 and i<j))}
 assert len(arcs)==t*(t-1)//2
 indeg=[sum((j,i) in arcs for j in range(t)) for i in range(t)]
 cores=[];last=0
 for x in indeg:
  cores.append(tuple(range(last,last+x+1)));last+=x+1
 n=last;fam=[]
 for i in range(t):
  targets=[j for j in range(t) if (i,j) in arcs]
  for values in itertools.product(*(cores[j] for j in targets)):
   F=frozenset(cores[i]+values);assert len(F)==t
   fam.append((i,F,sum(1<<v for v in F)))
 assert all(A&B for _,A,_ in fam for _,B,_ in fam)
 count=0
 for C in itertools.combinations(range(n),t-1):
  mask=sum(1<<v for v in C)
  assert any(not (mask&m) for _,_,m in fam)
  count+=1
 out.append(dict(t=t,k=t,n=n,members=len(fam),deficits=[t-len(X) for X in cores],sum_deficits=sum(t-len(X) for X in cores),checked_covers=count))
print(json.dumps(out,indent=2))
Path('workspace/agent3_rank_t_tournament_checks.json').write_text(json.dumps(out,indent=2))
'''
Path('workspace/agent3_rank_t_tournament_checks.py').write_text(code)

from pathlib import Path
text=r'''Owner-labelled sunflower compression lemma.
Assume disjoint cores Xi, residual ranks <=d, all original members pairwise intersecting. For P in class i, set E(P)=P union {label(j):P meets Xj}. Suppose E(P_1),...,E(P_L) is an ordinary sunflower, L>=d+2, with kernel K union labels(J), where K consists of actual vertices. Remove from J all owners of points in K, obtaining J0. For arbitrary choices y_j in Xj (j in J0), add G=Xi union K union {y_j:j in J0}. Its residual size <=|K|+|J0|<=d_i, because each original P must contain K and meet every Xj for j in J0, with these requirements requiring distinct vertices.

Claim G intersects every original member F in class h. If F meets Xi or K, immediate. If h in J, G meets Xh (either through K or y_h). Otherwise at most one sunflower branch has a point in Xh, since owner-label h is outside the kernel. Of remaining branches, if F misses Xi and K, each original Xi union P_l must intersect F through an actual tail point in F\Xh. These tails are pairwise disjoint and |F\Xh|<=d. There are L-1>=d+1 branches, impossible.

All additions, even from different sunflower choices and classes, are pairwise intersecting. Suppose added G_i and G_h disjoint. Its kernel data implies h notin J_i and K_i disjoint G_h; Xi also disjoint G_h. At most one branch of the first sunflower meets Xh, and at most d branches meet G_h\Xh. L>=d+2 leaves a branch whose original edge is disjoint G_h, contradicting the preceding claim that every added member meets every original member. Additions within the same class share Xi.

Adding these edges preserves covering number t: the old family is included, so tau cannot decrease; one core representative per class still covers, so tau cannot exceed t. This is valid for nonuniform residual rank <=d_i. After padding each Xi to cardinality >=t, covers of cardinality <t of a full product addition must hit Xi or K (unless hitting an actually fixed point already in K); they cannot exhaust an arbitrary target core Xj.
'''
Path('workspace/agent2_compression_lemma.txt').write_text(text)
print('Wrote precise proof to workspace/agent2_compression_lemma.txt')

code:
import itertools,z3,time,json
from pathlib import Path
start=time.time();t=6;k=8;d=2;c=k-d;n=t*c
cores=[frozenset(range(c*i,c*(i+1))) for i in range(t)]
F=[];owner=[];R=[];index={}
for i in range(t):
 for r in itertools.combinations(sorted(set(range(n))-cores[i]),d):
  index[i,r]=len(F);R.append(r);F.append(cores[i]|frozenset(r));owner.append(i)
M=[sum(1<<x for x in f) for f in F]
v=[z3.Bool('v'+str(a)) for a in range(len(F))]
s=z3.Solver();s.set(timeout=120000)
conf_count=0
for a in range(len(F)):
 for b in range(a):
  if owner[a]!=owner[b] and not M[a]&M[b]:
   s.add(z3.Or(z3.Not(v[a]),z3.Not(v[b])));conf_count+=1
print('conflicts',conf_count,'elapsed',time.time()-start,flush=True)
pattern=(c,2*c);s.add(v[index[0,pattern]])
count=0
V=set(range(n))
for Ct in itertools.combinations(range(n),t-1):
 hit={x//c for x in Ct};C=set(Ct);inds=[]
 for i in set(range(t))-hit:
  avail=sorted(V-cores[i]-C)
  inds.extend(index[i,r] for r in itertools.combinations(avail,2))
 s.add(z3.Or([v[a] for a in inds]));count+=1
 if count%50000==0:print('covers',count,'elapsed',time.time()-start,flush=True)
print('built all covers',count,'elapsed',time.time()-start,flush=True)
status=str(s.check());print('RESULT',status,'elapsed',time.time()-start,flush=True)
result={'t':t,'k':k,'core_size':c,'n':n,'status':status,'elapsed':time.time()-start,'pattern':pattern,'variables':len(F),'cover_clauses':count,'conflict_clauses':conf_count}
if status=='sat':
 model=s.model();fam=[sorted(f) for a,f in enumerate(F) if z3.is_true(model.eval(v[a]))]
 assert all(set(a)&set(b) for a,b in itertools.combinations(fam,2))
 assert all(any(not set(C)&set(f) for f in fam) for C in itertools.combinations(range(n),t-1))
 result['family']=fam
Path('workspace/agent2_t6_k8_distinct.json').write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2))
Path('workspace/agent2_t6_k8_distinct.py').write_text(Path('scratchpad.py').read_text())

Owner-labelled sunflower compression lemma.
Assume disjoint cores Xi, residual ranks <=d, all original members pairwise intersecting. For P in class i, set E(P)=P union {label(j):P meets Xj}. Suppose E(P_1),...,E(P_L) is an ordinary sunflower, L>=d+2, with kernel K union labels(J), where K consists of actual vertices. Remove from J all owners of points in K, obtaining J0. For arbitrary choices y_j in Xj (j in J0), add G=Xi union K union {y_j:j in J0}. Its residual size <=|K|+|J0|<=d_i, because each original P must contain K and meet every Xj for j in J0, with these requirements requiring distinct vertices.

Claim G intersects every original member F in class h. If F meets Xi or K, immediate. If h in J, G meets Xh (either through K or y_h). Otherwise at most one sunflower branch has a point in Xh, since owner-label h is outside the kernel. Of remaining branches, if F misses Xi and K, each original Xi union P_l must intersect F through an actual tail point in F\Xh. These tails are pairwise disjoint and |F\Xh|<=d. There are L-1>=d+1 branches, impossible.

All additions, even from different sunflower choices and classes, are pairwise intersecting. Suppose added G_i and G_h disjoint. Its kernel data implies h notin J_i and K_i disjoint G_h; Xi also disjoint G_h. At most one branch of the first sunflower meets Xh, and at most d branches meet G_h\Xh. L>=d+2 leaves a branch whose original edge is disjoint G_h, contradicting the preceding claim that every added member meets every original member. Additions within the same class share Xi.

Adding these edges preserves covering number t: the old family is included, so tau cannot decrease; one core representative per class still covers, so tau cannot exceed t. This is valid for nonuniform residual rank <=d_i. After padding each Xi to cardinality >=t, covers of cardinality <t of a full product addition must hit Xi or K (unless hitting an actually fixed point already in K); they cannot exhaust an arbitrary target core Xj.

from pathlib import Path
s=r'''Quadratic optimization / root facts (agent_3, coordinated agent_1).
Let petal candidates be vertices, with Kneser adjacency B_uv=1 iff u!=v and their petals are disjoint; diagonal B=0. Let A=J-B, so A_uv=1 iff petals intersect for distinct vertices, and A_uu=1 by convention. Maximize Q(mu)=sum_{u<v} B_uv mu_u mu_v subject to nonnegative weights with each color total1. Any original-core orientation bounds cross-color contribution by dt, and same-color contribution is at most1/2 per color, so Q<=dt+t/2.
One can choose a maximizer with pairwise DISJOINT petal supports inside each color: among maximizers minimize support; if two supported same-color petals intersect then B_uv=0 and Q is linear when shifting weight between u,v, so an endpoint is also optimal, contradiction. Thus A diagonal color blocks are identities on positive support.
For any direction z of totalweight0 in each color, supported on strictly positive coordinates, local maximality implies z^T B z<=0; since z^T J z=0, z^T A z>=0. Thus A is PSD on color-zero-sum subspace.
For root vectors e_u-e_v from same supported color, norm^2 under A equals2, and all pair innerproducts are integers in[-2,2]. Modulo nullspace this gives a positive-definite integral root lattice generated by norm2 roots; reflection closure is finite simply-laced ADE. This statement needs the usual finite root-lattice classification only if used further.
Dummy extension: add one dummy per color, all representing same new point p0, disjoint from all actual petals. If two colors have both dummy and actual positive support, roots r_u=e_u-e_dummy(i) satisfy norm^2=2, and cross-innerproduct=1+A_actual(u,v). If actual petals intersect, innerproduct2 forces equal roots; hence intersection among actual supported petals of dummy-mixed colors is an equivalence relation, and distinct classes consist of disjoint petals. This is rigorous but currently does not control colors with zero dummy weight.
'''
Path('workspace/agent3_qp_root_lemmas.txt').write_text(s)
print(s)

# Rigorous probability-bound checks for the counterexample to balanced-ground splitting.
# Analytic monotonicity handles every r>=1000: exp(.04r)/r^2 increases,
# and log(r/40)<=r/100 follows from value at1000 and derivative1/r<=.01.
checks={}
r=1000;n=r*r;t=n//20
checks['avoid_log_lower_safe']=math.log1p(-1/(20*(1-1/r))) >= -.06
checks['first_union_log_bound_negative']=n*math.log(2)+math.log(t)-math.exp(.04*r)<-1
checks['log_r_over_40_le_r_over_100']=math.log(r/40)<=r/100
checks['second_union_log_upper_coefficient']=math.log(2)+4*(.001+.01+.1-math.log(2))
checks['second_coefficient_negative']=checks['second_union_log_upper_coefficient']<0
assert all(v for k,v in checks.items() if isinstance(v,bool))
assert checks['second_union_log_upper_coefficient'] < -1
print(checks)
with open('workspace/agent4_balanced_split_counter_bounds.json','w') as f:json.dump(checks,f,indent=2)
with open('workspace/agent4_balanced_split_counter_bounds.py','w') as f:f.write(open(__file__).read())

from pathlib import Path
proof=r'''THEOREM. For all integers t>=2, b(t) <= t(3 ceil(t^(1/3))^2 - ceil(t^(1/3)) - 2). In particular limsup log b(t)/log t <=5/3.

Construction on T=h^3 classes (h>=2). Let n=2h^2 and let G be the disjoint union of h copies of K_{h,h}. Thus G is h-regular, has n vertices and T=h^3 edges. Classes are indexed by owner edges ab of G. Let W=E(K_n) be an actual ground-point set disjoint from all the cores. Write St(a) for the n-1 edges of K_n incident with a. Put r=n-h-1 and l=h^2-1. For class i=ab, define P_i to consist of every r-subset of St(a)\{ab} and every r-subset of St(b)\{ab}. Each P has a designated center a or b (indeed r>=2 makes it unique).

If P is centered at a, let O(P)={c!=a:ac notin P}; then |O(P)|=h. Let S(P) be the G-edges incident with at least one vertex of O(P), except the owner i. Since the other endpoint of i belongs to O(P), the owner was counted, so |S(P)|<=h^2-1=l. Extend S(P) arbitrarily to a set T(P) of exactly l owner classes excluding i. This is possible because T-1>=l.

Take pairwise disjoint cores X_i, each of size T, disjoint from W. For each P in P_i, include ALL sets X_i union P union {x_j:j in T(P)}, choosing x_j arbitrarily in X_j independently. Every member has cardinality k=T+r+l, and k-|X_i|=D=r+l=3h^2-h-2. A member of class i contains all X_i and at most one point of each other core, so the classes are pairwise disjoint as families.

Intersection. Same-class members share X_i. For distinct classes, if actual petals P,Q intersect, done. Otherwise their centers a,c cannot coincide, since 2r>n-1. Their only possible common actual point is ac, so ac is omitted from P or Q. In the first case c belongs to O(P), and Q's owner class (a G-edge incident with c) belongs to T(P). Hence the first member meets the entire core contained in the second member. The other case is symmetric.

Covering number. For a subset A of actual points W, let J(A) be the classes whose entire petal family P_i is met by A. If i=ab is in J(A), then A meets every r-subset of St(a)\{ab} and St(b)\{ab}. Since these ground sets have size n-2, both intersections with A have size at least (n-2)-r+1=h. In particular deg_A(a),deg_A(b)>=h. Let Z={a:deg_A(a)>=h}. Then |J(A)|<=e_G(Z)<=h|Z|/2<=|A| by regularity of G and the handshake lemma in the graph (V,A).

Now suppose C is a cover with |C|<T. Let A=C cap W, and B={i:C cap X_i nonempty}. Every core has T>|C| points. If i is outside B and some P in P_i avoids A, choose every target point x_j outside C; the resulting member avoids C, contradiction. Thus all T-|B| classes outside B belong to J(A), so T-|B|<=|A| and |C|>=|B|+|A|>=T, contradiction. One arbitrary representative from each core is a T-cover, so tau=T.

Arbitrary t. For h=ceil(t^(1/3)), T=h^3>=t. Retain any t of the T classes, with their existing cores and rank k. This subfamily has covering number exactly t: a cover of size<t, supplemented by one core representative from each omitted class, would cover the full construction with fewer than T points. Consequently b(t)<=tD. Since h=t^(1/3)+O(1), this proves the claimed exponent 5/3 upper bound.

Computational verification: workspace/agent2_clean_5over3_checks.py exhaustively checks all 4560 base-petal pairs for h=2, the exact degree criterion and |J(A)|<=|A| for all 1,683,218 actual-point subsets of size<T, and enumerates every one of the 49,152 resulting k=16 uniform members; it also explicitly constructs an uncovered member for 10,000 random purported full covers of size<T. Runtime7.6s in the actual environment. Earlier independent checks use h=2,3 clique-owner graphs.
'''
Path('workspace/agent2_upper_5over3_proof.txt').write_text(proof)
print('Saved complete all-integer upper-bound proof.')

## Fundamental normalizations and properties

Let petals
\[
\mathcal P_i=\{F\setminus X_i:F\in\mathcal F_i\}.
\]

1. Can enlarge \(X_i\) to full intersection of \(\mathcal F_i\), reducing cost. These full cores remain disjoint: a point common to two entire classes, plus one representative from each remaining core, gives a \(t-1\) cover.

2. Can **pad each core with arbitrarily many private class-only vertices**, uniformly across classes, increasing \(k\) and \(|X_i|\) equally, leaving all \(d_i\) unchanged and preserving \(\tau=t\). Thus large private cores are free.

3. For every class subset \(I\),
\[
\tau\Big(\bigcup_{i\in I}\mathcal F_i\Big)=|I|.
\]
Upper: one core rep each; lower: otherwise add reps outside \(I\), contradict \(\tau=t\).

4. Consequently for petals,
\[
\tau\Big(\bigcup_{i\in I}\mathcal P_i\Big)\ge |I|.
\]
Call this **petal Hall condition**.

5. Even stronger activation formulation: for any ground point set \(C\), number of classes whose **entire original class** (or entire petal family) is hit by \(C\) is at most \(|C|\).

6. Minimum covers of disjoint class subsets are disjoint. More generally if \(C_I,C_J\) are min covers of original class unions \(I,J\),
\[
|C_I\cap C_J|\le |I\cap J|,
\]
because union covers \(I\cup J\), whose \(\tau=|I\cup J|\). Slack #225/#226.

7. If \(v\in X_i\), remove class \(i\) and remove all members containing \(v\) from other classes. Remaining \(t-1\) classes nonempty, intersecting, and covering number exactly \(t-1\). Core/petal ranks unchanged. This is safe **owned-point conditioning** (#170).

8. Let \(Y_i\subset X_i\) be core points used in petals of other classes. For any \(F\in\mathcal F_i\), \(Y_i+(F\setminus X_i)+\) one private rep of \(X_i\) covers the whole family, hence
\[
|Y_i|\ge t-d_i-1,\qquad N_{\rm used}\ge t(t-1)-D.
\]
Thus hypothetical small-defect configurations need roughly \(t^2\) used core points, unlike typical high LP-gap hypergraphs on \(O(t)\) points. I posted #130. A normalization \(N_{\rm used}\le O(d^3)\) would imply \(t\le O(d^{3/2})\) and lower exponent \(5/3\); not proved.

9. Any original member is a transversal because family intersecting. If **\(k=t\)**, every member is a minimum transversal. For root edge \(F\) and \(S\subset F\),
\[
\mathcal H_S=\{E:E\cap F\subset S\}
\]
has \(\tau(\mathcal H_S)=|S|\): \(S\) covers it, and smaller cover + \(F\setminus S\) contradicts \(\tau=t\). Slack #255. No valid \(k\to t\) normalization is known.

## Rigorous universal lower bound \(b(t)=\Omega(t^{3/2})\)

Three agents derived independently; clean proof in `workspace/agent3_lower_proof.txt`.

Let total \(D\). At least \(m\ge t/2\) classes have \(d_i\le d=2D/t\) (can use floor/ceil carefully). Restrict to those classes (their full original union has \(\tau=m\), remains valid with \(k\ge m\)).

Choose a maximal **rainbow matching of petals**, \(R_i\in\mathcal P_i\), \(i\in I\), pairwise disjoint, \(r=|I|\).

- For any pair \(i,j\in I\), full members \(X_i\cup R_i,X_j\cup R_j\) intersect, cores disjoint, petals disjoint, so intersection must be \(R_i\cap X_j\) or \(R_j\cap X_i\).
- Each \(R_i\) meets at most \(d\) cores. Hence
\[
\binom r2\le rd,\quad r\le2d+1.
\]
- By maximality \(U=\bigcup R_i\) hits every petal of every unselected low-defect class. \(U\) plus one core rep for each selected class covers all \(m\) classes, so
\[
m\le rd+r=r(d+1)\le(2d+1)(d+1).
\]
This yields \(D\ge c t^{3/2}\), e.g. \(t^{3/2}/20\) for \(t\ge4\) was checked symbolically/numerically by agent_3. Files:

## BIG GENUINE BREAKTHROUGH: all-integer \(5/3\) upper

By agents_2 and _4, checked and fully written. **Read `workspace/agent2_upper_5over3_proof.txt` first.**

Clean parameters:
- Choose integer \(h\ge2\).
- \(n=2h^2\).
- Let \(G\) be disjoint union of **\(h\) copies of \(K_{h,h}\)**. It is \(h\)-regular on \(n\) centers and has
\[
T=|E(G)|=h^3.
\]
- Actual groundpoints \(A=E(K_n)\), i.e. unordered pairs of centers.
- Owner classes indexed by edges \(e=ab\in E(G)\).
- Put
\[
r=n-h-1=2h^2-h-1.
\]
- For class \(e=ab\), base petal types are ALL \(r\)-subsets of \(\operatorname{star}(a)\setminus\{ab\}\), and similarly all \(r\)-subsets of \(\operatorname{star}(b)\setminus\{ab\}\).
  Think petal \(P\) centered at \(a\). Its omitted center set
\[
O(P)=\{c\ne a: ac\notin P\}
\]
has size \(h\), and includes \(b\).

### Hall/activation property of base petals
For actual point set \(C\subset E(K_n)\), it hits **every** centered-at-\(a\) petal for owner \(ab\) iff
\[
\deg_C(a)-{\bf1}_{ab\in C}\ge h.
\]
It hits full class \(ab\) iff this holds at BOTH endpoints.
If \(S\) are vertices with \(\deg_C(a)\ge h\), every covered owner edge lies in \(G[S]\). Thus
\[
\#\{\text{whole base classes hit by }C\}
\le |E(G[S])|\le h|S|/2\le |C|.
\]
This is the petal Hall condition, and enough for final \(\tau=T\).

### Intersecting completion using target cores
For petal \(P\) centered \(a\), target all owner edges of \(G\) incident with centers in \(O(P)\), **except its own class**. There are at most \(h^2-1\) targets. Fill arbitrarily with other class labels to get EXACTLY \(h^2-1\) target classes (possible \(T-1\ge h^2-1\)).

Add huge pairwise disjoint cores \(X_e\) of size \(T\) (or sufficiently large); final members in class \(e\):
\[
X_e\cup P\cup\{ \text{one arbitrary point from each target core}\}.
\]
Thus fixed residual size
\[
d=r+h^2-1=3h^2-h-2,
\]
uniform rank \(k=T+d\).

Why intersecting:
- Same center actual petals intersect since \(2r>n-1\).
- Different centers \(a,c\): actual petals meet only potentially at point \(ac\). If they do not meet, at least one omits the other center. That petal targets EVERY owner edge incident that center, including other's owner class, and hits other's whole core.

Why \(\tau=T\):
- One rep per class covers.
- For any cover \(C\) size <T, let \(A=C\cap E(K_n)\), and let \(I\) be core classes met by \(C\). By activation inequality, actual \(A\) fully hits at most \(|A|\) classes. Since \(|I|+|A|<T\), choose class \(e\notin I\) with base petal \(P\) avoiding \(A\). Core \(X_e\) avoids C, and each arbitrary target choice can avoid C since each core size T>|C|. Thus a final member avoids C.

Therefore
\[
b(h^3)\le h^3(3h^2-h-2).
\]
For **arbitrary \(t\)** take \(h=\lceil t^{1/3}\rceil\), build \(T=h^3\), and **restrict to ANY t classes**. Full subunion covering number exactly t (otherwise add outside class core reps to cover original T-family with <T). Rank k remains ≥t and cores remain. Cost ≤t d, giving
\[
b(t)\le(3+o(1))t^{5/3}.
\]

Every pair of disjoint petals of different colors has a core-petal intersection in original family, so orient KG edge toward other color if petal meets that other's core. Each vertex has **outneighbor COLORS ≤d**.

Conversely (agent_4 #182):

## QP / root-system framework (rigorous lemmas, main lower avenue)

Agent_3 wrote `workspace/agent3_qp_root_lemmas.txt`.

Let disjointness graph D on all petals (or augmented petals). Assign nonnegative weights w_P with **sum within each color =1**, maximize total Kneser edge energy \(Q\), including same-color pairs. Every **pure representative choice** has crosscolor disjoint pairs ≤dt by original core-target orientation; withincolor contribution ≤t/2, so universally
\[
Q\le (d+1/2)t.
\]

A maximizer can be chosen with within-each-color support a **matching** (pairwise disjoint petals):
- If two intersecting same-color petals have positive mass, moving mass between them has linear objective, so eliminate one without decreasing Q.
- At global maximum KKT: all supported petals in color i have same weighted disjoint degree \(\lambda_i\); every original alternate petal of that color has degree ≤λ_i.

Second-order condition I noticed:
- Let A be **intersection indicator matrix**, diagonal1.
- On subspace of perturbations with total weight0 in every supported color, A is PSD (because D quadratic is NSD there).
- For samecolor supported u,v (disjoint), formal root \(e_u-e_v\) has squared norm2.
- Inner products of all such roots are integers in \{-2,-1,0,1,2\}.
- After quotient nullspace and reflection closure, get finite simply-laced ADE root lattice! Agent_3 #209 validated.
- Large color support gives A_{L−1} subsystem; possibly root classification can force graphic/star structure. Main problem: many colors may have singleton support, no root directions.

### Dummy trick
Add to each color one dummy representing the same new point p0, disjoint from every actual petal; dummies mutually intersect. Can weight dummy–actual edges by M.

If total actual mass R, dummy D=t−R, objective
\[
M R D+Q_{\rm actual}.
\]

For M=1 and **ALL colors mixed dummy/actual**, roots \(e_P-e_{\rm dummy}\) have norm²2; cross inner =1+A_actual(P,Q), so intersecting actual supports give inner2 => equal root. Thus supported actual petals split into disjoint intersection cliques. KKT gives:
- each cluster actual mass =D,
- R=kD, t=(k+1)D,
- \(Q_{\rm actual}=t² k(k−1)/(2(k+1)²)\).
If t≫d, Q≤dt forces k=1; KKT then every original petal meets every support actual petal, giving d-point cover all t colors, impossible. So counterexamples must have many pure colors.

Small M refinement (agents2/3/4):
- Take M=C d/t (<1/4, C>4) so baseline forces R,D=Ω(t).
- Scaling all actual weights down gives
\[
\delta=M(R-D)\le 2d+1.
\]
- Any original petal of a pure-dummy color has disjoint actual mass ≤δ.
- Mixed actual roots norm²2M; cross inner =2M−1 if actual supports disjoint, violates Cauchy for M<1/4. Hence **each mixed color has one supported actual petal and all mixed supported petals intersect / roots equal**.
- For pure-actual matching support u,v, inner(u−v,mixed root) integer but abs≤2√M<1, so0: all support petals of each pure-actual color have identical intersection status with mixed petals.
- Therefore can redistribute actual masses arbitrarily among mixed colors holding total mixed actual mass R_m fixed and stay optimal.
- KKT for any dummy-positive original petal P must hold for every redistribution:
  \[
  b_{\rm pure}(P)+\min(R_m,\#\{\text{mixed supported }E_i:P\cap E_i=\emptyset\})\le\delta
  \]
  (exclude own if relevant).
  If R_m>δ, P misses at most floorδ mixed supported petals **unweighted**.
- Pure-color issue unresolved. I suggested homotopy varying M: if supports pure/unit, threshold δ gives selected actual D-subgraph min degree≥ceilδ, while all original pure-dummy petals have degree≤floorδ. At integer δ critical colors can mix; could assemble root-system “k-core phases” and derive r√d via phase count. Slack #269.

## External-point pruning / bad coalitions (CURRENT main possible φ mechanism)

For **petal Hall** families \(\mathcal P_i\), and actual point v, delete all petals containing v:
\[
\mathcal P_i^0=\{P\in\mathcal P_i:v\notin P\}.
\]
Define bad class subset I if
\[
\tau\left(\bigcup_{i\in I}\mathcal P_i^0\right)<|I|.
\]
Original Hall implies any bad I has τ exactly |I|−1 (adding v covers removed petals). **Any two disjoint bad subsets impossible**: covers of them plus v would violate original Hall on union. Thus minimal bad coalition family \(B_v\) is intersecting on color labels.

Let
\[
\lambda_v=\tau(B_v)
\]
= minimum #classes to discard to restore Hall after avoiding v.

- For owned core point v∈Xi, in original full configuration λ≤1 via safe deletion/conditioning.
- For unowned external v, λ can exceed1. Explicit Fano6-line example from agent3 #272:
  - cores Xi={xi}, i=1,2,3;
  - external v,q12,q13,q23.
  - class i has
    \(A_i=\{x_i,v,q_{jk}\}\),
    \(B_i=\{x_i,q_{ij},q_{ik}\}\).
  - all6 edges intersect, τ3.
  - avoid v leaves3 B-triangle edges τ2; deleting ANY single class then τ1, not2.
  - minimal bad coalitions {12},{13},{23}, hitting number2.

Potential bootstrap:
- If one proves **\(b(\lambda_v)\le O(d)\)** for these bad coalition systems (or special variant), known b(s)≥s^α gives pruning cost λ≤d^{1/α}.
- Energy/pruning might then yield t≤d·d^{1/α}, leading improved b exponent
  \[
  \alpha\mapsto 2-\frac1{\alpha+1}.
  \]
  Starting 3/2: 8/5,21/13,... →φ.
- Converse external-point extension realizing any b(h) as a bad-coalition gadget might supply upper recursion replacing h² by b(h), hence φ.
- This is only a **mechanism**, no lemma proved. Both agents2/4 investigating.
- A **naive** “max rainbow matching r ⇒ b(r)≤Cd” minor is FALSE from a single unselected class: start regular tournament r old classes with huge cores, add new class whose petals are all minimum covers of old family (rank r), τ becomes r+1, maxdefect r but b(r)~r². Need MANY unselected classes/t≫d if any minor lemma.

Naive upper recursion h²→b(h) has a serious **single-omission obstacle**:
- In star construction, P centered a omits ac, Q centered c may NOT omit ac.
- P must then intersect all Q owner cores at c, since Q does not activate inner petal at pair(a,c).
- Inner intersecting gadget only helps when BOTH sides activate. Making every member pay inner petals for all centerpairs costs n·b(h)/h and ruins improvement.
- Absorbing omitted inner core blocks into outer cores leads conflicting ownership of actual point ac between two outer classes, and often n≥sum inner cores≈h².
- Agents2/4 explicitly agreed recursion not automatic (#250/#251). Do not claim φ upper yet.

### Graph universal obstruction
Pure graph domination / defective Haxell is insufficient.
Vertices (i,S), |S|=d, i∉S, each color class clique, crosscolor **intersection graph** adjacency iff j∉S and i∉T. Nonedges can orient from chooser, outneighbor colors≤d. Any transversal has ≤td nonedges, hence very dense for t=d². Yet domination of color union ≈min(|I|,d+1), satisfying ≥|I|/d for t≤d².
Thus cannot derive desired bounds using only colorful domination. Need rank-r intersection representation / local clique cover.
Also disproves hoped generic connectivity scaling of bounded-degree independence complexes \(K_D\sim D\gamma\).

Naive projective plane petals have cheap external blocking sets O(q) or O(q logq), so τ far below q² target. Labels at unique line intersections forced globally equal, also cheap covers. Extending lines with omitted-point repairs gives deficit O(q) but still double-blocking cover O(q logq).

import itertools,z3,time,json
start=time.time();h=2;n=2*h*h
G=[]
for block in range(h):
 L=list(range(2*h*block,2*h*block+h));R=list(range(2*h*block+h,2*h*(block+1)))
 G += [(a,b) for a in L for b in R]
actual=list(itertools.combinations(range(n),2));eid={e:j for j,e in enumerate(actual)};t=len(G)
families=[]
for a,b in G:
 fam=[]
 for c,other in [(a,b),(b,a)]:
  star=[eid[tuple(sorted((c,x)))] for x in range(n) if x not in (c,other)]
  fam += [tuple(P) for P in itertools.combinations(star,n-h-1)]
 families.append(fam)
res=[]
for vpair in [(0,2),(0,1),(0,4)]:
 v=eid[vpair];pruned=[[P for P in fam if v not in P] for fam in families]
 vs=[z3.Bool('x%d'%i) for i in range(len(actual)+t)];bad=[]
 for mask in range(1,1<<t):
  I=[i for i in range(t) if mask>>i&1]
  s=z3.Solver()
  s.add(z3.PbLe([(x,1) for x in vs],len(I)-1))
  for i in I:
   for P in pruned[i]:s.add(z3.Or(vs[len(actual)+i],*[vs[p] for p in P]))
  if s.check()==z3.sat:bad.append(mask)
 minimal=[b for b in bad if not any(c!=b and c&b==c for c in bad)]
 assert all(a&b for a in minimal for b in minimal)
 hits=[]
 for k in range(t+1):
  hits=[T for T in itertools.combinations(range(t),k) if all(any(b>>i&1 for i in T) for b in minimal)]
  if hits:break
 item=dict(point=vpair,bad_count=len(bad),minimal_bad=[[i for i in range(t) if b>>i&1] for b in minimal],lambda_v=k,min_hitting_sets=hits)
 res.append(item);print(item,flush=True)
with open('workspace/agent4_star_badcoalitions_h2.json','w') as f:json.dump({'owners':G,'results':res},f,indent=2)
with open('workspace/agent4_star_badcoalitions_h2.py','w') as f:f.write(open(__file__).read())
print('elapsed',time.time()-start)

### General bad-coalition argument to finish

Setup clean star construction below. Petal families \(\mathcal P_i\) on actual points \(E(K_n)\), \(G\) \(h\)-regular, owner colors \(i=ab\in E(G)\). \[
d_S(a)-1_{\{ab\in S\}}\ge h-1_{\{a\in v,\ ab\ne v\}},

- \(|J(S)|\le e_G(W)\le h|W|/2\).

from pathlib import Path
text=r'''A simpler upper construction: duplicate center colors.

Let m,n be positive integers with n>4m-1. Put T=nm and r=n-2m.
Let the actual points be the edges of K_n. There are m colors/classes for
each center a in [n]. Give every class i its own disjoint T-point core X_i,
outside all actual points.

For every r-subset P of the (n-1)-edge star at a, let O(P) be the 2m-1
other centers b such that ab is omitted from P. Let L(P) be all m classes
at every center in O(P), so |L(P)|=ell=m(2m-1).
For each class i centered at a, include every set
 X_i union P union {x_j:j in L(P)},
where all choices x_j in X_j are independent. The rank is
 k=T+r+ell=T+n+2m^2-3m,
and every deficit equals D=n+2m^2-3m.

Distinct classes give distinct sets, as one set contains its complete own
T-point core and at most one point of each other core. Every class is
nonempty. All cores are disjoint and nonempty.

Intersection: same-class members share their core. Same-center petals
intersect since 2r>n-1. For different centers a,b, disjoint petals force
at least one to omit actual point ab. If P at a omits ab, it includes
one representative of every class at b, hence intersects the full core
of the other member.

Covering number: selecting one representative of each core gives a
T-point cover. Conversely suppose |C|<T. No core is exhausted. Let
A be C's actual edges, and B the classes whose cores C meets. For each
class outside B, its whole petal family must be met by A, because any
petal disjoint from A can have all its independent target-core choices
made outside C. A hits every r-subset of center a's (n-1)-edge star iff
d_A(a)>=n-r=2m. Thus, writing Z={a:d_A(a)>=2m},
 T-|B| <= m|Z| <= (1/2)sum_{a in Z}d_A(a) <= |A|.
But |C|>=|A|+|B|, a contradiction.

Taking n=m^2, m>=4, gives T=m^3, D=3m^2-3m. For arbitrary large t take
m=ceil(t^(1/3)) and keep any t classes. Every subunion of t classes has
covering number t: a cover of size<t could be supplemented with one
core representative per omitted class to cover the whole original
family in fewer than T points. Therefore
 b(t)<=t(3 ceil(t^(1/3))^2-3 ceil(t^(1/3)))=(3+o(1))t^(5/3).

The asymptotic leading constant from this construction can be optimized:
take n=4m^2, giving T=4m^3, D=6m^2-3m and constant 6/4^(2/3).

Actual checks: workspace/agent2_duplicate_center_checks.py/.json.
For m=1,n=4: all 64 actual edge subsets, all 48 final members, all 1794
possible covers of size<4 checked. For m=2,n=8: all 560 colored base
petals and all 156520 pairs checked; all 1213 graphical degree sequences
checked for Hall degree charge; 20000 random actual point sets checked
for exact activation against enumerated petals.
'''
Path('workspace/agent2_duplicate_center_upper_proof.txt').write_text(text)
print('saved proof, bytes',len(text))

import itertools,json,time
from pathlib import Path
st=time.time(); r=7; N=2*r-1; v=N-1
Q={1,2,4}
def beats(a,b):return (b-a)%r in Q
edges=[]; classes=[[] for _ in range(r)]
for E in itertools.combinations(range(N),r):
 S=[a for a in E if a<r]
 opts=S if len(S)==1 else [a for a in S if any(beats(b,a) for b in S if b!=a)]
 i=min(opts); e=sum(1<<x for x in E); classes[i].append(e); edges.append(e)
assert all(classes)
for i,cl in enumerate(classes):
 core=(1<<N)-1
 for e in cl:core&=e
 assert core==1<<i
zero=[[e for e in cl if not(e>>v&1)] for cl in classes]
# All possible covers C of v-free edges: masks on N-1 vertices.
cover_cost=[N]* (1<<r)
for C in range(1<<(N-1)):
 A=sum(1<<i for i,cl in enumerate(zero) if all(e&C for e in cl))
 c=C.bit_count(); sub=A
 while True:
  cover_cost[sub]=min(cover_cost[sub],c)
  if not sub:break
  sub=(sub-1)&A
bad=[I for I in range(1,1<<r) if cover_cost[I]<I.bit_count()]
minimal=[I for I in bad if not any(J!=I and J&I==J for J in bad)]
lam=min(T.bit_count() for T in range(1<<r) if all(T&I for I in minimal))
gamma=min(T.bit_count() for T in range(1<<r) if all(any((T>>b&1) and (b==a or beats(b,a)) for b in range(r)) for a in range(r)))
assert gamma==3 and lam>=gamma
Ias=[sum(1<<b for b in range(r) if b==a or beats(b,a)) for a in range(r)]
assert all(I in bad for I in Ias)
assert all(I&J for I in minimal for J in minimal)

from pathlib import Path
text=r'''Point-pruning bad coalitions in the regular-owner star construction.

Let G be an h-regular graph on n centers. Each owner color is an edge
ab in E(G). Its petal family consists of all r=(n-h-1)-subsets of
St(a) minus {ab}, and all such subsets of St(b) minus {ab}, where actual
points are E(K_n). Adjoin a private core label c_i to every petal of
color i; assume r>=1. Original colored Hall follows by degree charge.

Fix an actual point v=xy, and remove all petals containing v. For an
actual set S not containing v, let J(S) be colors whose entire remaining
petal family is met by S. Exactly,
 ab in J(S) iff
 deg_S(a)-1_{ab in S} >= h-1_{a in {x,y}, ab != v},
 deg_S(b)-1_{ab in S} >= h-1_{b in {x,y}, ab != v}.
(The formulas follow from the transversal number of all r-subsets of a
q-point set being q-r+1.) In particular old Hall plus one removed point
gives |J(S)|<=|S|+1.

A color coalition I becomes bad precisely when some actual S has
|I intersect J(S)|>|S|, since all other colors in I can be covered by
one private core label each. Consequently every minimal bad coalition
is J(S) with |J(S)|=|S|+1.

For such S let W be endpoints of J(S). Every a in W has
 deg_S(a)>=h-1_{a in {x,y}}.
Thus
 2|J(S)| <= h|W| <= 2|S|+2.
The assumed equality |J(S)|=|S|+1 forces equality throughout. It follows
that x,y are in W; J(S)=E_G(W); every G-neighbor of any W-vertex is in W
(so W is a union of whole connected components of G); all S-edges have
both endpoints in W; and degrees in S are h except at x,y, where they
are h-1. No edge of G can belong to S, since any activated own edge in S
would raise a required endpoint degree above these forced values.

If v belongs to G, its entire component is in W, so v itself is an
activated owner. But this owner's threshold remains h at x and y,
contradicting their forced S-degrees h-1. Thus there are NO bad coalitions.
If v does not belong to G, every minimal bad coalition contains every
owner edge of x's component (and y's component). Therefore any single
color in x's component meets every bad coalition. The minimum number
lambda_v of colors to discard to restore Hall is at most 1.

This proves lambda_v=0 for owner actual points and lambda_v<=1 otherwise,
for every h-regular G where the construction is defined. No assertion
of existence of bad coalitions in the latter case is needed.

Independent exhaustive checks for h=2, G=2K_{2,2}: all actual S of size
at most 7 were enumerated for each of the 3 actual-point symmetry orbits.
Owner v: no bad coalition; nonowner v in one component and across two
components: the sole minimal bad coalition is all 8 colors, lambda_v=1.
See workspace/agent2_star_badcoalitions_h2.py/.json; independently checked
by agent_4 via all 256 color coalitions and SAT cover calculations.
'''
Path('workspace/agent2_star_badcoalitions_proof.txt').write_text(text)
print('saved',len(text))

import itertools,z3,time,random,json
start=time.time();rng=random.Random(34567)
h=3;n=2*h*h
G=[]
for block in range(h):
 L=range(2*h*block,2*h*block+h);R=range(2*h*block+h,2*h*(block+1));G += [(a,b) for a in L for b in R]
actual=list(itertools.combinations(range(n),2));eid={e:j for j,e in enumerate(actual)};inc=[[i for i,e in enumerate(actual) if a in e] for a in range(n)]
def compute(deleted,colors):
 cs=[z3.Bool('c%d'%p) for p in range(len(actual))];ys={i:z3.Bool('y%d'%i) for i in colors}
 solver=z3.Solver()
 for p in deleted:solver.add(z3.Not(cs[p]))
 for i in colors:
  a,b=G[i];ab=eid[a,b]
  for x in (a,b):
   threshold=h-len(set(inc[x])&deleted)+(ab in deleted)
   solver.add(z3.Implies(ys[i],z3.PbGe([(cs[p],1) for p in inc[x] if p!=ab],threshold)))
 solver.add(z3.PbGe([(y,1) for y in ys.values()]+[(c,-1) for c in cs],1))
 def findbad(allowed):
  if solver.check(*[z3.Not(ys[i]) for i in colors if i not in allowed])==z3.unsat:return None
  model=solver.model();I=[i for i in colors if z3.is_true(model.eval(ys[i]))]
  return I
 cuts=[];opt=z3.Optimize();ds={i:z3.Bool('d%d'%i) for i in colors};opt.minimize(z3.Sum([z3.If(x,1,0) for x in ds.values()]))
 while True:
  assert opt.check()==z3.sat;model=opt.model();drop=[i for i in colors if z3.is_true(model.eval(ds[i]))]
  bad=findbad(set(colors)-set(drop))
  if bad is None:return drop,cuts
  for i in list(bad):
   sub=findbad(set(bad)-{i})
   if sub is not None:bad=sub
  cuts.append(bad);opt.add(z3.Or([ds[i] for i in bad]))
results=[]
for trial in range(12):
 colors=list(range(len(G)));deleted=set();order=list(range(len(actual)));rng.shuffle(order)
 for p in order:
  if not colors:break
  deleted.add(p);drop,cuts=compute(deleted,colors)
  item=dict(trial=trial,point=actual[p],deleted=[actual[v] for v in sorted(deleted)],colors=colors[:],drop=drop,lambda_v=len(drop),cuts=cuts)
  results.append(item)
  if len(drop)>1:print('trial',trial,'depth',len(deleted),'colors',len(colors),'lambda',len(drop),flush=True)
  colors=[i for i in colors if i not in drop]
print('maxlambda',max(x['lambda_v'] for x in results),'runtime',time.time()-start,flush=True)
with open('workspace/agent4_random_pruning_star_h3.json','w') as f:json.dump(dict(h=h,G=G,results=results),f,indent=2)
with open('workspace/agent4_random_pruning_star_h3.py','w') as f:f.write(open(__file__).read())

Any original-core orientation bounds cross-color contribution by dt, and same-color contribution is at most1/2 per color, so Q<=dt+t/2.

code: @agent_3 Simple useful support-cover observation in dummy QP: every pure-dummy candidate petal misses ≤δ actual-support MASS, with R>δ. Therefore ANY point cover U of the actual supported petals automatically covers ALL pure-dummy classes (otherwise a candidate avoiding U misses full mass R). Thus τ(pure-dummy classes) ≤ τ(actual support). If actual support has only singleton colors, Q≤O(dt) immediately gives an actual-supported petal disjoint from only O(d) other supported petals; that petal + one point from each disjoint support covers all support in r+O(d), closing this case. Remaining obstacle specifically weighted multi-support pure-actual colors (tiny weights), not singleton pure-actual colors by themselves.

from pathlib import Path
proof=r'''CORE-IDENTIFICATION NORMALIZATION LEMMA

Given a valid k-uniform t-class configuration with disjoint nonempty
cores X_i, call x in X_i used if it belongs to a member of a class other
than i. Let N be the total number of used core points.

For any distinct v,w in the same core X_i, there is a uniformity-preserving
identification operation, preserving all core cardinalities, with new
covering number t-1 exactly when some old minimum t-cover contains both
v and w, and new covering number t otherwise. In the latter case it is
a valid configuration with exactly the same deficits. If v,w are used,
its number of used core points is at most N-1.

PROOF. First form the quotient q that identifies v,w to a fresh z and
fixes every other point. For the quotient family Q, t-1<=tau(Q)<=t:
old covers map to covers, and a quotient cover lifts to an old cover by
replacing z, if present, by v,w. Moreover tau(Q)=t-1 iff an old minimum
t-cover contains both v,w. The forward direction follows by lifting a
(t-1)-cover; it must use z and its lift is a t-cover. The reverse
direction follows by applying q to such an old t-cover.

The quotient members of class i have size k-1, as they contain both v,w;
other members have size k unless they originally contained both v,w.
Adjoin a fresh private point u to every quotient member of class i.
The new core is X_i'=(X_i minus {v,w}) union {z,u}; other cores are fixed.
This private-core addition leaves the quotient covering number unchanged:
any cover using u can replace it by z without increasing its cardinality,
and every cover of Q remains a cover after the addition.

Every remaining short (k-1)-member E belongs to a class j!=i. Replace E
by all k-sets E union {a}, a in R, where R is a fresh reservoir of t+1
points outside all cores. (The same R may serve all short members.)
Call the resulting set-family H. Its covering number equals tau(Q),
because every old quotient cover covers H, whereas any H-cover C of size
at most t misses some a in R; for each short E the member E union {a}
then forces C to meet E. Covers of cardinality>t cannot be minimal since
we already have a quotient cover of size<=t. Thus H has covering number
t or t-1 according to the exact criterion above.

Identification, private additions, and padding all preserve intersection.
The displayed core sizes and rank k are unchanged. Different source
classes may now have duplicate members: assign each distinct member to
any one source class that produced it. It still contains that source's
core. If tau(H)=t, no resulting class can be empty, because otherwise one
representative of each remaining core would cover H in at most t-1
points. Thus this deduplication gives a valid partition into t nonempty
classes. Deficits k-|X_j| are unchanged.

If v,w were used, their two contributions to N are replaced by at most
the one used point z. The point u occurs only in class i, so is unused;
reservoir points lie outside cores; no other core point gains an occurrence
in another class. Deduplication can only remove occurrences. Hence N
decreases at least one. QED.

CONSEQUENCE. Every valid configuration can be replaced, at no increase of
any deficit, by one satisfying simultaneously:
 (1) every class core is its entire common intersection;
 (2) the total family is edge-minimal subject to covering number t;
 (3) every pair of distinct used points in any one core occurs together
     in some minimum t-cover of the whole family.

Indeed repeatedly perform (a) any permitted same-core merge of a used
pair not lying together in any minimum cover; (b) deletion of any edge
whose deletion preserves tau=t; (c) enlargement of a core to its full
common intersection. Full class intersections are pairwise disjoint:
a point common to two would cover both classes, and representatives of
other cores would give a (t-1)-cover. Consequently enlargement is valid
and only decreases deficits. Deleting edges cannot empty a class while
preserving tau=t. It also cannot destroy the pair-cooccurrence property,
since old minimum covers remain covers of size t.

Termination can be formalized by the lexicographic potential (D,N,M),
where D=sum deficits, N=#used core points, and M=#family members. An
enlargement strictly lowers D; a merge keeps D and strictly lowers N
(though M may increase from padding); a criticality deletion keeps D,
does not increase N, and strictly lowers M if N is unchanged. These are
nonnegative integers, and at each operation rank k and t are fixed, so
D and N are globally bounded; there are finitely many (D,N) decreases,
and between them only finitely many edge deletions. Thus the process
terminates, with (1)--(3).

ACTUAL CHECKS: workspace/agent2_core_identification_checks.py/.json.
All 24 same-core pair merges in the 4-class/48-edge duplicate-center
instance were checked by enumeration of all minimum covers and all new
covers up to size4; criterion predicted tau correctly in every case.
A 2-class example with an outside member containing BOTH merged points
checks the all-reservoir padding step, including duplicate quotients.
A second 2-class example checks the obstruction: a pair in an old
minimum cover produces tau=t-1 after identification.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT PROVE: No polynomial bound on N in the normalized
configuration is presently established. In particular N=O(d^3) for
maximum deficit d, which would give the desired 5/3 lower bound using
N>=t(t-d-1), is NOT proved here.
'''
Path('workspace/agent2_core_identification_normalization.txt').write_text(proof)
print('saved',len(proof))

# Symmetry: one edge 0,1,2,3 belongs.
s.add(vs[0])
conflicts=0
for i,e in enumerate(masks):
 for j in range(i):
  if not e&masks[j]:s.add(z3.Or(z3.Not(vs[i]),z3.Not(vs[j])));conflicts+=1
for C in itertools.combinations(range(n),r-1):

from pathlib import Path
proof=r'''GENERALIZED RANK NORMALIZATION (agent3)

A generalized configuration has t disjoint nonempty cores Xi and nonempty
colored classes Fi of sets Xi union P, with P disjoint Xi and |P|<=di.
The union is intersecting and has covering number t; duplicated edges across
colors are harmless and may be assigned to any source color. No color can
then become empty, since its omission would give a (t-1)-core cover.

The minimum of sum di over generalized configurations equals b(t).
One inequality is immediate. Conversely choose K>max_i(|Xi|+di). Add private
core points so new |Xi|=K-di. For each old petal P of size <di add ALL
(di-|P|)-subsets of a fresh reservoir Z of size max_i di+t. Old full edges
embed in every resulting edge, so intersection remains. Core representatives
cover in t points. A putative cover of <t new points can be normalized by
replacing any new private core point with an old core point of that color;
this does not increase its size or lose any covered member. Reservoir choices
can avoid this cover, since |Z\C|>=max_i di+1. Thus the normalized old-ground
part would cover every old member with fewer than t points, impossible.
All resulting edges have rank K, and deficits are exactly di.

Therefore choose a generalized minimizer of D=b(t), and among those choose
one of minimum total ground size. Merge two points v,w whenever they are not
in distinct cores. Core nonemptiness/disjointness and petal rank budgets are
preserved; intersection is preserved under quotient. For this quotient,
covering number drops iff some old minimum t-cover contains BOTH v,w:
- such a cover quotients to a (t-1)-cover;
- a quotient cover with <t lifts to a cover of at most t old points, by
  replacing the merged point with {v,w}; it must have exactly t-1 points,
  contain the merged point, and lift to a minimum old t-cover containing both.
If covering number did not drop, the quotient would be a generalized
configuration of the same deficit budget but smaller ground size, contradiction.
Hence EVERY pair not lying in distinct cores co-occurs in a minimum t-cover.
This includes all external-external pairs and external-core pairs.

Additional deletion consequence: all core points are used by another color,
except possibly the sole point of a singleton core. Otherwise delete an
unused core point (non-singleton case); all intersections and t-cover property
survive. Every external point and every non-singleton core point has a private
crosspair of full members whose sole intersection is that point: otherwise
its deletion preserves intersection, petals only shrink, and remaining cores
still supply a t-cover. Such a private pair must have distinct source colors.

This is a proved normalization only. It does NOT yet bound ground size or
used core points by O(d^3); that remains the missing lower-bound theorem.
'''
Path('workspace/agent3_global_merge_normalization.txt').write_text(proof)
from itertools import combinations
cores=[{0,1,2},{3,4}]
classes=[[set(cores[0])],[set(cores[1])|{v} for v in cores[0]]]
H=sum(classes,[]);V=set.union(*H)
def covers(H):
 V=set.union(*H)
 for s in range(len(V)+1):
  C=[set(C) for C in combinations(sorted(V),s) if all(set(C)&E for E in H)]
  if C:return s,C
oldtau,B=covers(H)
assert oldtau==2
records=[]
for v,w in combinations(sorted(V),2):
 if any(v in X for X in cores) and any(w in X for X in cores) and not any({v,w}<=X for X in cores):continue
 HH=[{v if x==w else x for x in E} for E in H]
 newtau,_=covers(HH)
 criterion=any({v,w}<=C for C in B)
 assert (newtau<oldtau)==criterion
 records.append(dict(pair=[v,w],tau_new=newtau,pair_in_mincover=criterion))
import json
Path('workspace/agent3_global_merge_checks.json').write_text(json.dumps(records,indent=2))
print('Verified generalized pair-merge criterion on',len(records),'pairs; preserving and dropping examples:',records)
print('Proof saved.')

from pathlib import Path
text=r'''SATURATED GLOBAL-MINIMUM-GROUND NORMALIZATION
(Refinement of agent_3's generalized rank-budget normalization.)

A generalized configuration consists of t disjoint nonempty cores X_i
and t nonempty colored subfamilies of an intersecting family H with
tau(H)=t, where every member of class i contains X_i and has at most d_i
points outside it. Uniformity is not imposed. Its cost is sum_i d_i.
The minimum possible cost equals b(t).

For the nontrivial direction, choose K>=max_i(|X_i|+d_i). Adjoin private
points to each core until its size is K-d_i. This leaves tau unchanged:
a cover using a new private point can replace it by any old point of the
same nonempty core, and old covers still cover. Pad each short residual
P of class i to size d_i by ALL choices of the requisite number of
points from a fresh common reservoir R, with |R|>t+max_i d_i. Rank becomes
K. Intersections persist. A proposed cover of size<t misses enough
reservoir points to choose a padding disjoint from it, so it must cover
every unpadded old member. Thus tau stays t. Deduplicate source classes
arbitrarily; no class can vanish when tau=t, since representatives of
the remaining cores would be a (t-1)-cover. This gives a valid original
uniform configuration of cost sum_i d_i.

Among generalized configurations of optimal cost b(t), choose one with
minimum total ground size n=|V|. On this fixed ground, choose one with
maximum number of distinct family members. Such choices exist by integer
well-ordering and finiteness of 2^V. We may discard isolated vertices,
so V is precisely the union of all members.

NORMALIZATION A. Every pair of distinct points of V belongs together
to some minimum t-cover of H.

Proof: If points are in different cores, choose them and one arbitrary
representative of each other core. This is a t-cover. Every other pair
can be identified while maintaining disjoint nonempty cores and without
increasing any residual rank budget. Identification preserves
intersection. As in the core-identification lemma, its new covering
number is t-1 iff the old points co-occur in a minimum t-cover, and is t
otherwise. In the latter case deduplicate source classes; if any class
vanished, fewer than t core representatives would cover. Thus a missing
co-occurrence pair would yield a valid configuration of no greater cost
on n-1 points; if cost dropped this contradicts optimal b(t), otherwise
it contradicts minimal n. This proves A.

NORMALIZATION B. If a set E subseteq V contains some full core X_i,
|E minus X_i|<=d_i, and intersects every old member, then E already
belongs to H (possibly assigned to another class).

Proof: Otherwise add E to class i. This does not increase any budget;
intersection persists; old H still forces tau>=t, while core
representatives still give tau<=t. Ground size is unchanged. Thus this
would contradict maximality of the number of members.

from pathlib import Path
text=r'''REDUCED CORES AND EXACT RANK EXCESS IN THE DUPLICATE-CENTER UPPER

Use the duplicate-center construction with m>=2, n>4m-1,
 T=nm, r=n-2m, ell=m(2m-1), D=r+ell=n+2m^2-3m.
All actual petals, target labels, and independent choices are as in
workspace/agent2_duplicate_center_upper_proof.txt. The sole change is
that every core has size c=T-n+1=n(m-1)+1, not T.
Then c>T/2 and the uniform rank is
 k=c+D=T+2m^2-3m+1.
Thus rank excess s=k-T=2m^2-3m+1, independent of n.
Intersection and disjoint classes follow exactly as before (c>=2).

We prove tau=T. Core representatives give a T-point cover. Suppose
|C|<T. Let A be its actual edge points and B the classes whose cores it
meets but does not exhaust. Since c>T/2, C exhausts at most one core.
If none is exhausted, the original Hall degree proof applies verbatim.

Suppose one exhausted core belongs to a class centered at b. For any
other center a!=b, if C does not meet the core of some class i centered
at a, an uncovered final member exists unless either deg_A(a)>=2m or
actual edge ab belongs to A. Indeed, otherwise the star at a has at
least r available points outside A and includes available ab. Choose
an r-subset P containing ab and avoiding A. This petal does not target
ANY class at center b, so avoids the exhausted core, and all other
target-core representatives can be chosen outside C.

Partition the n-1 centers a!=b into three kinds:
 (i) ab in A; their number is the count of A-star edges at b;
 (ii) ab notin A, deg_A(a)>=2m;
 (iii) neither condition, so ALL m class cores at a must be met by C.
For type (ii), every A-edge incident with a is a non-star edge (its
other endpoint is not b); summing degrees shows their number is at
most |A_nonstar|/m. Type (iii) centers number at most |B|/m. Consequently
 n-1 <= |A_star|+(|A_nonstar|+|B|)/m <= |A|+|B|.
Therefore |C|>=c+|A|+|B|>=c+n-1=T, contradiction.

There is in fact a T-cover consisting of one whole core centered at b
plus the full actual star at b, of size c+n-1=T. At center b the actual
star meets every petal; at any other center a, a petal either contains
ab and is hit by the star, or omits ab and targets every class at b,
so is hit by the exhausted core.

Thus the reduced-core construction is valid for all stated m,n. Taking
n=4m^2 yields T=4m^3,D=6m^2-3m, rank excess s=2m^2-3m+1. Taking n=m^2
and m>=4 yields T=m^3,D=3m^2-3m with the same rank excess. The cost and
5/3 exponent are unchanged, while the rank-excess tradeoff is explicit.

ACTUAL CHECK: m=2,n=8 gives T16,c9,r4,ell6,D10,k19,s3. Every one of
1,683,218 actual edge sets A of size<=7 was enumerated. The exact count
of partial core representatives additionally necessary after exhausting
one fixed core was computed from the activation formula, and
 |A|+required_partial >=7
was checked in every case, with equality achieved. Symmetry covers all
choices of exhausted core. Source/results:
 workspace/agent2_reduced_core_upper_checks.py/.json.
'''
Path('workspace/agent2_reduced_core_upper_proof.txt').write_text(text)
print('saved',len(text))

from pathlib import Path
text=r'''COMPATIBLE STRONG NORMAL FORM: SATURATION OF CORE-EXHAUSTING
MINIMUM COVERS AND RESIDUAL-POINT PRIVATE INTERSECTIONS

Work in the generalized rank-budget model (same optimum b(t)). Choose
an optimal-cost configuration on the minimum possible total number of
points. Thus every pair of distinct points co-occurs in a minimum
t-cover, by the global merge lemma. All cores are already their full
class intersections: otherwise enlargement by one common point would
reduce that class's maximum residual rank and lower the optimal cost;
common intersections of different classes cannot overlap since tau=t.

First add allowed intersecting members on the existing ground until
saturated. By the previous lemma, every minimum t-cover C containing
an entire core is now itself a family member. Global optimal cost and
minimum ground size remain in force, so every pair still co-occurs in
a minimum t-cover. Every rank budget stays the same: if an operation
permitted a strict decrease, it would contradict optimal b(t).

Now repeatedly perform either of these operations:
 (a) delete a member containing a different member (inclusion redundancy);
 (b) delete a residual point p from a member F whenever doing so preserves
     intersection with every other member.
Both operations preserve tau=t: (a) does not change covers, and (b)
can only increase the covering number, while core representatives still
cover with t points. Intersection and the source core condition hold.
Any duplicate members can be assigned to an arbitrary source class;
none can empty when tau=t. Cost and minimum ground size remain optimal.
Operation (b) strictly decreases total member size, and (a) decreases
member count/total size, so the process terminates.

The core-exhausting-minimum-cover property survives. Indeed deletion
of inclusion-redundant edges leaves the whole cover family unchanged;
shrinking a member can only REMOVE covers, never create a new cover.
Hence every final minimum t-cover C that exhausts a core was already
a minimum cover immediately after saturation, and so was an actual
rank-t member then. Such a member can never be shrunk while preserving
intersection, since a smaller intersecting member would itself be an
all-family cover of size<t. Nor can it be inclusion-redundant under a
smaller member, for the same reason. Thus C persists as an actual edge.

At termination every residual point p of every edge F has another
edge E with F intersect E={p}; otherwise p could be deleted. The witness
cannot be F itself: another member must become disjoint when p is
removed. If a residual point were essential only to self-intersection,
then F minus {p} would remain nonempty because it contains a nonempty
core, and self-intersection would persist as well.

Consequently an optimal minimum-ground generalized configuration can
be chosen satisfying simultaneously:
 1. every class core equals its whole common intersection;
 2. every point pair co-occurs in some minimum t-cover;
 3. every core-exhausting minimum t-cover is an actual family member
    (so such covers form an intersecting family);
 4. every residual occurrence has a private singleton intersection witness;
 5. no member properly contains another.

CAVEAT: ordinary tau-edge-critical pruning is NOT included, because
it can create new minimum covers which need not be actual members.
This normal form does not yet bound the ground size by O(d^3).
'''

print('saved',len(text))

from itertools import combinations
from z3 import *
from pathlib import Path
import json,time
out=[]
for n in (8,9,10):
 r=3;E=[frozenset(e) for e in combinations(range(n),r)]
 x=[Bool('x%d_%d'%(n,i)) for i in range(len(E))]
 b=[Bool('b%d_%d'%(n,i)) for i in range(len(E))]
 s=Solver();s.set(timeout=60000)
 for i,A in enumerate(E):
  for j in range(i):
   if not A&E[j]:s.add(Or(Not(x[i]),Not(x[j])))
 for C in combinations(range(n),r-1):
  C=set(C);s.add(Or([x[i] for i,A in enumerate(E) if not A&C]))
 for i,C in enumerate(E):s.add(b[i]==And([Not(x[j]) for j,A in enumerate(E) if not A&C]))
 for P in combinations(range(n),2):
  P=set(P);s.add(Or([b[i] for i,C in enumerate(E) if P<=C]))
 # Valid anchors edge012 and edge034 private against {1,2}; label symmetry.
 s.add(x[E.index(frozenset((0,1,2)))])
 s.add(x[E.index(frozenset((0,3,4)))])
 t=time.time();ans=s.check();R=dict(n=n,rank=3,result=str(ans),seconds=time.time()-t)
 if ans==sat:
  m=s.model();H=[sorted(A) for i,A in enumerate(E) if is_true(m.eval(x[i]))]
  B=[sorted(C) for i,C in enumerate(E) if is_true(m.eval(b[i]))]
  R.update(edges=H,mincovers=B)
  from scipy.optimize import linprog
  import numpy as np
  M=np.zeros((n,len(B)))
  for j,C in enumerate(B):M[C,j]=1
  lp=linprog(np.zeros(len(B)),A_eq=M,b_eq=np.ones(n),bounds=(0,None),method='highs')
  R['polar_fpm']=lp.success
 out.append(R);print(R,flush=True)
Path('workspace/agent3_mincover_pairshadow_rank3.py').write_text(Path('scratchpad.py').read_text())
Path('workspace/agent3_mincover_pairshadow_rank3.json').write_text(json.dumps(out,indent=2))

from pathlib import Path
text=r'''PARTIALLY REPEATED CORE POINTS HAVE THREE-OWNER PRIVATE PAIRS

Use the fully saturated generalized fixed-budget normal form: every
set containing a full core, within that class's residual rank budget,
and intersecting all old members is already an actual family member.
Let C be a minimum t-cover. Suppose a core X_i is partially met by C,
with 2<=|C intersect X_i|<|X_i|.

Then for EVERY v in C intersect X_i, every private cover-witness edge
E with E intersect C={v}, and every u in X_i minus C, there is another
edge G such that E intersect G={v}, u notin G, and the owner classes of
X_i,E,G are three distinct classes.

Proof. A private witness E exists because C is a minimum (hence
irredundant) cover. Its owner j differs from i, since an edge of class i
contains all of C intersect X_i, which has at least two points. Hence v
is residual in E. Put E'=(E minus {v}) union {u}. This contains X_j and
is within the residual budget of class j, even if u was already in E;
moreover E' is disjoint from C. If E' intersected every actual edge,
saturation would force E' itself to be an actual edge, contradicting
that C covers the family. Thus some G is disjoint from E'. Since the
original family is intersecting and E minus E' is contained in {v},
E intersect G={v}. Owner(G) cannot be i, because every class-i member
contains u; nor can it be j, because every class-j member contains the
nonempty X_j subset E'. This proves the assertion.

Thus, if a point v in a core X_i is never the unique intersection of
two edges BOTH owned outside i, it cannot appear in a partially repeated
nonexhausted core part of a minimum cover. Every minimum cover containing
v and another X_i point must exhaust X_i. This is an exact restricted
version of the conjectural partial-core classification.

ACTUAL CHECK: applied to agent_4's saturated rank4 tau4 family on9
points, cores (3,2,2,2). Enumerated ALL52 minimum4-covers, all partially
repeated core parts, every private witness E, and every permitted u.
All29 resulting cases have explicit G certificates with three distinct
owners. Files workspace/agent2_partial_cover_private_checks.py/.json.

MISSING: No bound is proved on the number of these three-owner-private
exceptional core points in a minimum-ground configuration.
'''
Path('workspace/agent2_partial_cover_private_lemma.txt').write_text(text)
print('saved',len(text))

start=time.time();loc=json.load(open('workspace/agent4_partial_cover_saturation.json'))[0]['family'];t=6
cores=[{17},{18,19}];lcores=[{0,1,2,9,10},{3,4,11,12},{5,6,13,14},{7,8,15,16}];cores+=lcores
oldl=[{0,1,2},{3,4},{5,6},{7,8}];LH=[]
for e in loc:
 e=set(e);i=next(i for i,X in enumerate(oldl) if X<=e);LH.append(lcores[i]|(e-oldl[i]))
outer=[{17,18},{17,19},{18,19}];H=LH[:]
for e in outer:
 for choices in itertools.product(*[sorted(X) for X in lcores]):H.append(e|set(choices))
def mask(E):return sum(1<<v for v in E)
H=list(set(mask(E) for E in H));C=mask({17,18,0,1,3,5});arr=np.array(H,dtype=np.int64)
assert all((C&e)!=0 for e in H)
for c in itertools.combinations(range(20),5):assert np.any((arr&mask(c))==0)
assert all(np.all((arr&e)!=0) for e in H)
# Saturate among all rank6 allowed members.
allowed=[]
for e in itertools.combinations(range(20),6):
 E=set(e)
 if any(X<=E for X in cores):allowed.append(mask(E))
added=0
for e in allowed:
 if e in H:continue
 if all(e&f for f in H):
  assert e&C
  H.append(e);added+=1
arr=np.array(H,dtype=np.int64)
assert all(e in H or np.any((arr&e)==0) for e in allowed)
assert all(e&C for e in H)
assert all(any((e&f)==(1<<p) for f in H) for e in H for p in range(20) if e>>p&1)
for X in cores:
 F=[e for e in H if (e&mask(X))==mask(X)];intersection=(1<<20)-1
 for e in F:intersection&=e
 assert intersection==mask(X)
assert not any((C&mask(X))==mask(X) for X in cores)
assert (C&mask(lcores[0])).bit_count()==2
out=dict(t=t,n=20,cores=[sorted(X) for X in cores],initial_edges=len(set(mask(e) for e in LH))+960,final_edges=len(H),added=added,allowed=len(allowed),cover=[p for p in range(20) if C>>p&1],all_5_covers_rejected=15504,all_residual_private=True,full_cores=True,saturated=True,runtime=time.time()-start)
print(out,flush=True)
with open('workspace/agent4_join_partial_cover_checks.json','w') as f:json.dump(out,f,indent=2)
with open('workspace/agent4_join_partial_cover_checks.py','w') as f:f.write(open(__file__).read())

from itertools import combinations,product
from pathlib import Path
import json,time
import z3

def tournament(t):
 out=[[] for _ in range(t)]
 for i,j in combinations(range(t),2):
  # cyclic regular for odd; nearly regular restriction for even
  n=t if t%2 else t+1
  a,b=(i,j) if (j-i)%n<=n//2 else (j,i)
  out[a].append(b)
 ind=[sum(i in out[j] for j in range(t)) for i in range(t)]
 cores=[];n=0
 for v in ind:cores.append(set(range(n,n+v+1)));n+=v+1
 classes=[]
 for i in range(t):
  classes.append([frozenset(cores[i]|set(p)) for p in product(*(cores[j] for j in out[i]))])
 return cores,classes,n

def check(t):
 start=time.time();X,H,n=tournament(t)
 ds=[t-len(x) for x in X];d=max(ds);k=t+2*d
 Y=[];N=n
 for di in ds:Y.append(set(range(N,N+k-2*di)));N+=k-2*di
 # All old points are actual copies 0..n-1. Reservoir used for q<di.
 Z=list(range(N,N+t+d));N+=len(Z)
 HH=[]
 for i,cl in enumerate(H):
  target=[]
  for F in cl:
   P=set(F)-X[i];owners=[j for j in range(t) if P&X[j]]
   for choices in product(*(Y[j] for j in owners)):
    for pad in combinations(Z,ds[i]-len(owners)):
     E=frozenset(Y[i]|P|set(choices)|set(pad));assert len(E)==k
     target.append(E)
  HH.append(list(set(target)))
 E=[e for cl in HH for e in cl]
 assert len(set(E))==len(E)
 for i,F in enumerate(E):
  assert all(F&G for G in E[:i])
 assert all(Y[i]<=e and len(e-Y[i])==2*ds[i] for i,cl in enumerate(HH) for e in cl)
 assert all(not(Y[i]&Y[j]) for i,j in combinations(range(t),2))
 s=z3.Solver();s.set(timeout=60000);v=[z3.Bool('v%d_%d'%(t,i)) for i in range(N)]
 s.add(z3.PbLe([(q,1) for q in v],t-1))
 for e in E:s.add(z3.Or([v[p] for p in e]))
 status=str(s.check());assert status=='unsat'
 canonical={min(y) for y in Y};assert all(e&canonical for e in E)
 return dict(t=t,old_n=n,old_core_sizes=list(map(len,X)),old_class_sizes=list(map(len,H)),old_deficits=ds,k=k,s=k-t,new_core_sizes=list(map(len,Y)),new_class_sizes=list(map(len,HH)),new_n=N,new_edges=len(E),intersection_pairs=len(E)*(len(E)-1)//2,small_cover_status=status,seconds=time.time()-start)
results=[check(t) for t in (3,4,5)]
print(json.dumps(results,indent=2))
Path('workspace/agent3_rank_excess_normalization_checks.json').write_text(json.dumps(results,indent=2))
Path('workspace/agent3_rank_excess_normalization_checks.py').write_text(Path('scratchpad.py').read_text())

members. Put T=|W|. This constructs T colored actual-petal families of
rank at most M+1 with Hall transversal inequalities. It DOES NOT by

small out-target assignment is supplied.

Take a fresh point v and pairwise disjoint blocks Q_F of size k-1,
one for each F in B. For every x in W define H_x by two types:
 A_x = all sets choosing exactly one point of each Q_F with x in F;
 B_x = all sets {v} union a choice of one point of each Q_F with x notin F.
Use the ordinary convention that a product over no blocks is {empty}.

EXACT ACTIVATION. For any actual point set S, let E={F: Q_F subset S},
and write U=union(E), I=intersection(E), with U=empty,I=W if E=empty.
A_x is entirely hit by S iff x in U. If v in S, B_x is always hit;
otherwise B_x is entirely hit iff x notin I. Consequently the set of
colors whose WHOLE H_x is hit is U if v in S, and U\I otherwise.

HALL. For h=|E|, |U|<=h(k-1)+1 because the inner members intersect.
Also |U\I|<=h(k-1): if I is nonempty, remove its s>=1 points from each
member and use |U\I|<=h(k-s). If I is empty, expose members successively.
Every new member meets the previous union. At the FIRST step when the
running common intersection becomes empty, the new member meets the
previous union in at least TWO points: if its only union point were p,
its intersection with every earlier member would force p into their
common intersection. This gives |U|<=k+(h-1)(k-1)-1=h(k-1).
Thus when v in S, |S|>=1+h(k-1)>=|U|; when v notin S,
|S|>=h(k-1)>=|U\I|. In either case activated colors <=|S|.
Equivalently, for every J subset W, tau(union_{x in J} H_x)>=|J|.

PRUNING v. Delete all petals containing v, leaving exactly A_x.
A coalition J is now bad iff its union of colored petal families has
transversal number <|J|. A cover S activates U as above, and costs at
least h(k-1). If |J|>|S| and J subset U, then |U|<=h(k-1)+1 forces
J=U, |J|=h(k-1)+1, and J contains some inner member F. Conversely, if
F subset J, exhausting the single block Q_F, of cost k-1, covers all
colors of F, and adding one point from any petal-transversal for each
remaining color would not be justified in full generality; for MINIMAL
bad coalitions we instead note F itself is bad, with cover Q_F.
Hence every bad coalition contains an F in B, and each F itself is
bad. The inclusion-minimal bad coalitions are EXACTLY B.

cores/petals must reprove activation-Hall, as well as furnish original

text=r'''RAINBOW SELF-PETALS OBSTRUCT A TARGET-COMPLETION OF FACTORED REVERSE

Let an inner family H be partitioned into T classes with disjoint cores
X_i. Choose one anchor a_i in each core. In the factored reverse gadget,
label the private Q_i (size |X_i|-1) by X_i minus {a_i}; write q_{i,x}.
Each residual point x in an inner member of class j is copied as p_{j,x},
with these copies shared WITHIN owner j and disjoint across owners.
Thus Q_F=Q_owner union {p_{owner,x}: x in F minus X_owner}.

For every nonanchor corepoint x in X_i minus {a_i}, form
 S_x={q_{i,x}} union {p_{j,x}: j!=i and some F in H_j contains x}.

CLAIM: S_x is an inclusion-minimal transversal of
 {Q_F: F in H and x in F}. Hence S_x is an actual TYPE-A petal of the
 reverse color x.
Proof: for F of owner i, its Q_i contains q_{i,x}. For F of any other
 owner j containing x, its residual copy contains p_{j,x}. Conversely,
 every chosen point of S_x belongs to one private owner-ground block.
 That owner block has some relevant F, and S_x has exactly ONE point
 in that block, so this F witnesses indispensability of that point.
This proves both hitting and minimality.

All the S_x are PAIRWISE DISJOINT for distinct nonanchor x: their Q_i
labels and residual-copy labels differ. Thus the reverse gadget has a
rainbow actual-petal matching of size
 q=sum_i(|X_i|-1).

Consider ANY proposed intersecting-core realization that keeps these
actual petals and adds only points in disjoint own/target cores (or
uses uniformity padding from which disjoint choices can be selected).
Take the corresponding q full members. Their own cores are mutually
disjoint, as are their actual S_x. Each pairwise intersection therefore
requires a residual core-target slot of one endpoint. A residual slot
can target only ONE of the other disjoint cores, and hence accounts
for at most one pair. Consequently
 binom(q,2) <= sum_{x selected} d_x,
and in particular max_x d_x >=(q-1)/2.

This statement is NOT about arbitrary modifications of the actual
petal system: adding common actual points can destroy the matching,
but may also destroy Hall. It directly obstructs economical target
completion of the fixed factored reverse system.

Cloning every old point L times and replacing each inner occurrence by
the whole clone-pack does NOT fix this: the same proof gives one
self-petal per nonanchor cloned corepoint, so
 q=L*sum_i|X_i|-T.
In the regime |X_i|>=T-d with d=o(T), q is asymptotic to L*T^2.
Thus target completion needs maximum deficit Omega(L*T^2), not O(T*d)
or O(T*L). The tempting golden-ratio reverse recursion cannot be
implemented by this unmodified factored reverse architecture.

        out[a].append(b)
    indeg=[sum(i in out[j] for j in range(T)) for i in range(T)]
    X=[];c=0
    for d in indeg:
        X.append(set(range(c,c+d+1)));c+=d+1
    oldH=[];own=[]
    for i in range(T):
        for p in product(*(sorted(X[j]) for j in out[i])):
            oldH.append(X[i]|set(p));own.append(i)
    # Clone-pack blowup of all old points.
    X=[{L*x+a for x in C for a in range(L)} for C in X]
    H=[{L*x+a for x in F for a in range(L)} for F in oldH]
    qlabel={};nextpoint=0
    for i,C in enumerate(X):
        for x in sorted(C)[1:]:qlabel[i,x]=nextpoint;nextpoint+=1
    copies={};Q=[]
    for F,i in zip(H,own):
        B={p for (j,x),p in qlabel.items() if j==i}
        for x in sorted(F-X[i]):
            if (i,x) not in copies:copies[i,x]=nextpoint;nextpoint+=1
            B.add(copies[i,x])
        assert len(B)==T*L-1
        Q.append(B)
    selfpetals={}
    for (i,x),q in qlabel.items():
        S={q}|{p for (j,y),p in copies.items() if y==x}
        conditional=[B for B,F in zip(Q,H) if x in F]
        assert conditional and all(S&B for B in conditional)
        assert all(any(S&B=={p} for B in conditional) for p in S)
        selfpetals[x]=S

    q=len(selfpetals)
    assert q==sum(map(len,X))-T
    return dict(inner_classes=T,clones=L,inner_edges=len(H),inner_rank=T*L,

                checked_self_petals=q,all_self_pairs=q*(q-1)//2,
                maximum_self_rank=max(map(len,selfpetals.values())),
                target_completion_maxdef_lower=(q-1)/2)

print(json.dumps(rows,indent=2))
