from pathlib import Path
text=r'''COMPATIBLE ALL-CHOICE NORMAL FORM WITH A RANK-t MEMBER IN EVERY CLASS

Pure separated generalized model. Each class i has a disjoint core X_i;
a base pattern is (P,T), where P is an actual point set disjoint from all
cores and T is a subset of other class labels. Its full members are
X_i union P union {x_j:j in T}, for ALL independent choices x_j in X_j.
Assume |P|+|T|<=d_i<=d, the full family is intersecting, and tau=t.
Suppose t>2d. Initially core sizes can be arbitrary (the usual factor-2
normalization may be used to arrange this model with large cores).

THEN, without increasing any residual cap d_i, one can modify this
model so that all-choice symmetry is retained and:
 (1) t-d_i<=|X_i|<=t for every class;
 (2) each class i contains some ACTUAL rank-t members of form
 C_i=X_i union A_i union {x_j:j in L_i}, for ALL choices x_j in X_j,
 where |A_i|+|L_i|=t-|X_i|<=d_i.
The whole resulting family still has covering number t and is
intersecting. Its other members may have size greater than t.

IRREDUNDANT COVERS. A partially, but not fully, met core contributes
only to covering its OWN class. Indeed, a foreign base pattern has at
most one independently chosen point in that core; a choice outside the
partial cover avoids it. Thus an irredundant cover meets every
nonexhausted core in at most one point.

SYMMETRIC CORE MERGE. Identify two points a,b of X_i, retaining all
independent target choices. Intersection is preserved and no residual
budget increases. The new covering number is either t or t-1, and it
is t-1 iff some old minimum t-cover contains BOTH a,b: map such a cover
to the quotient; conversely lift a new cover of size<t, replacing the
merged point by both preimages if necessary, to get an old cover of
size at most t. By the preceding fact, an old minimum cover containing
a,b must EXHAUST X_i.

LOCKING ALGORITHM. Keep some classes locked. To lock an unlocked i,
merge pairs in X_i while tau remains t, stopping as soon as there is a
minimum t-cover C exhausting X_i. Such a stop must occur: every class
has an edge of size at most |X_i|+d_i, and any edge of an intersecting
family covers it, so throughout |X_i|>=t-d_i>t/2>=1. Hence one cannot
merge forever, and a first forbidden merge supplies C. This cover
exhausts NO other core, since all core sizes exceed t/2. Consequently
irredundancy gives C=X_i union A union one point from each core in L,
with |A|+|L|=t-|X_i|<=d_i.

ALL CHOICE VARIANTS OF C ARE COVERS. Classes i and those in L are met
through their own cores. For h outside L union {i}, an actual pattern
(P,T) must either have i in T or P meet A: otherwise choose its target
points in every partially met core outside C, giving an old member
disjoint from C. This contradicts that C is a cover. This condition
also shows that every alternative choice of the points in L is a cover.
Add all these variants as members of class i. They meet every old
member because they are old covers, and meet each other in X_i.
Their residual size is t-|X_i|<=d_i. Adding members cannot decrease
tau, and any new rank-t member covers the enlarged intersecting family,
so tau remains exactly t. Lock i.

Later merges are only in UNLOCKED cores. A previously added rank-t
member has at most one point in any such foreign core, so its rank
stays t under a merge; all choices remain available and intersection
is preserved. Thus its lock persists. Repeat at most t times. The
finite total ground shrinks between locking steps, proving termination.
No edge can acquire two owners: a class-h edge has at most d_h<=d
points outside X_h, while every other core has >t/2>d points.

USEFUL CONSEQUENCE. For every original/current base pattern (P,T) of
class h outside L_i union {i}, P meets A_i OR i is in T. Thus these
rank-t seeds give short dual certificates as well as pairwise
intersecting actual members. They do NOT by themselves make all old
members rank t, nor prove a binomial or 5/3 lower bound.
'''
Path('workspace/agent2_allchoice_rankt_seed_normalization.txt').write_text(text)

from pathlib import Path
import json,time

def allchoice_tournament(coresizes):
    t=len(coresizes);out=[[] for _ in range(t)]
    for i,j in combinations(range(t),2):
        n=t if t%2 else t+1
        a,b=(i,j) if (j-i)%n<=n//2 else (j,i)
        out[a].append(b)
    X=[];n=0
    for c in coresizes:X.append(set(range(n,n+c)));n+=c
    H=[];owners=[]
    for i in range(t):
        for P in product(*(sorted(X[j]) for j in out[i])):
            H.append(sum(1<<x for x in X[i]|set(P)));owners.append(i)
    return X,H,owners,n,out

def exactcovers(X,H,n,t):
    covers=[];xm=[sum(1<<x for x in C) for C in X]
    tested=0
    for r in range(t+1):
        for cc in combinations(range(n),r):
            tested+=1;C=sum(1<<x for x in cc)
            if all(C&F for F in H):
                assert r==t,(r,t)
                for K in xm:
                    assert C&K==K or (C&K).bit_count()<=1
                covers.append(C)
    assert covers
    return covers,tested

start=time.time();cs=[5]*5;locked=[];rows=[]
for i in range(5):
    while True:
        X,H,own,n,out=allchoice_tournament(cs)
        assert all(F&G for F,G in combinations(H,2))
        C,tested=exactcovers(X,H,n,5)
        xm=sum(1<<x for x in X[i]);exhaust=[c for c in C if c&xm==xm]
        rows.append(dict(core_sizes=cs[:],selected_class=i,edges=len(H),ground=n,
                         subsets_tested=tested,minimum_covers=len(C),exhausts_selected=bool(exhaust)))
        if exhaust:
            seed=exhaust[0];A=[];L=[]
            for j,K in enumerate(X):
                hit=[x for x in K if seed>>x&1]
                if j!=i and hit:L.append(j)
            variants=[xm|sum(1<<x for x in choices) for choices in product(*(sorted(X[j]) for j in L))]
            assert all(v.bit_count()==5 for v in variants)
            assert all(v&F for v in variants for F in H)
            assert all(v&w for v,w in combinations(variants,2))
            # All variants here are already original edges, as expected for tournaments.
            assert set(variants)<=set(H)
            locked.append(i);break
        cs[i]-=1
assert cs==[3]*5
# Explicit rank-t seed addition check in nontrivial duplicate-center upper family.
m=2;n=8;T=m*n;c=T-n+1;r=n-2*m;ell=m*(2*m-1);D=r+ell
E=list(combinations(range(n),2));edgeid={e:j for j,e in enumerate(E)}
stars=[{edgeid[tuple(sorted((a,b)))] for b in range(n) if a!=b} for a in range(n)]
base=[]
for owner in range(T):
    a=owner//m
    for pp in combinations(sorted(stars[a]),r):
        P=set(pp);omitted=[b for b in range(n) if b!=a and edgeid[tuple(sorted((a,b)))] not in P]
        targets={m*b+s for b in omitted for s in range(m)}
        assert len(targets)==ell
        base.append((owner,P,targets))
seedchecks=0
for i in range(T):
    a=i//m;Ai=stars[a]
    assert c+len(Ai)==T and len(Ai)<=D
    for h,P,target in base:

        seedchecks+=1
    for j in range(i):assert Ai&stars[j//m]
summary=dict(tournament=dict(stages=rows,final_core_sizes=cs,classes_locked=locked,

             nontrivial_star_seed_addition=dict(t=T,core_size=c,old_member_rank=c+D,new_seed_rank=T,
                   base_patterns=len(base),seed_old_pattern_checks=seedchecks,new_seed_pairs=T*(T-1)//2),
             runtime=time.time()-start)
print(json.dumps(summary,indent=2))
Path('workspace/agent2_allchoice_rankt_seed_checks.json').write_text(json.dumps(summary,indent=2))

COMPATIBLE ALL-CHOICE NORMAL FORM WITH A RANK-t MEMBER IN EVERY CLASS

Pure separated generalized model. Each class i has a disjoint core X_i;
a base pattern is (P,T), where P is an actual point set disjoint from all
cores and T is a subset of other class labels. Its full members are
X_i union P union {x_j:j in T}, for ALL independent choices x_j in X_j.
Assume |P|+|T|<=d_i<=d, the full family is intersecting, and tau=t.
Suppose t>2d. Initially core sizes can be arbitrary (the usual factor-2
normalization may be used to arrange this model with large cores).

THEN, without increasing any residual cap d_i, one can modify this
model so that all-choice symmetry is retained and:
 (1) t-d_i<=|X_i|<=t for every class;
 (2) each class i contains some ACTUAL rank-t members of form
 C_i=X_i union A_i union {x_j:j in L_i}, for ALL choices x_j in X_j,
 where |A_i|+|L_i|=t-|X_i|<=d_i.
The whole resulting family still has covering number t and is
intersecting. Its other members may have size greater than t.

IRREDUNDANT COVERS. A partially, but not fully, met core contributes
only to covering its OWN class. Indeed, a foreign base pattern has at
most one independently chosen point in that core; a choice outside the
partial cover avoids it. Thus an irredundant cover meets every
nonexhausted core in at most one point.

SYMMETRIC CORE MERGE. Identify two points a,b of X_i, retaining all
independent target choices. Intersection is preserved and no residual
budget increases. The new covering number is either t or t-1, and it
is t-1 iff some old minimum t-cover contains BOTH a,b: map such a cover
to the quotient; conversely lift a new cover of size<t, replacing the
merged point by both preimages if necessary, to get an old cover of
size at most t. By the preceding fact, an old minimum cover containing
a,b must EXHAUST X_i.

LOCKING ALGORITHM. Keep some classes locked. To lock an unlocked i,
merge pairs in X_i while tau remains t, stopping as soon as there is a
minimum t-cover C exhausting X_i. Such a stop must occur: every class
has an edge of size at most |X_i|+d_i, and any edge of an intersecting
family covers it, so throughout |X_i|>=t-d_i>t/2>=1. Hence one cannot
merge forever, and a first forbidden merge supplies C. This cover
exhausts NO other core, since all core sizes exceed t/2. Consequently
irredundancy gives C=X_i union A union one point from each core in L,
with |A|+|L|=t-|X_i|<=d_i.

ALL CHOICE VARIANTS OF C ARE COVERS. Classes i and those in L are met
through their own cores. For h outside L union {i}, an actual pattern
(P,T) must either have i in T or P meet A: otherwise choose its target
points in every partially met core outside C, giving an old member
disjoint from C. This contradicts that C is a cover. This condition
also shows that every alternative choice of the points in L is a cover.
Add all these variants as members of class i. They meet every old
member because they are old covers, and meet each other in X_i.
Their residual size is t-|X_i|<=d_i. Adding members cannot decrease
tau, and any new rank-t member covers the enlarged intersecting family,
so tau remains exactly t. Lock i.

Later merges are only in UNLOCKED cores. A previously added rank-t
member has at most one point in any such foreign core, so its rank
stays t under a merge; all choices remain available and intersection
is preserved. Thus its lock persists. Repeat at most t times. The
finite total ground shrinks between locking steps, proving termination.
No edge can acquire two owners: a class-h edge has at most d_h<=d
points outside X_h, while every other core has >t/2>d points.

USEFUL CONSEQUENCE. For every original/current base pattern (P,T) of
class h outside L_i union {i}, P meets A_i OR i is in T. Thus these
rank-t seeds give short dual certificates as well as pairwise
intersecting actual members. They do NOT by themselves make all old
members rank t, nor prove a binomial or 5/3 lower bound.

this does NOT rule out an original maximum-deficit-two example at t=6.

A pattern of class i is (P,T), actual set P, foreign target-label set T,
with |P|+|T|<=d. All independent one-point choices from target cores
occur. In any putative example with t>=6,d<=2, every core has size at
least t-d>=4 (any member covers an intersecting family). Thus for two
patterns of DIFFERENT owners i,j the exact intersection condition is
 P intersect Q nonempty OR j in T OR i in U.                 (*)
Indeed any shared third-core choices can be chosen distinct.

LEMMA 1 (cap one). A valid full-Hall instance with d<=1 has t<=3.
If all actual patterns are nonempty, they are target-free singletons;
cross-class intersection forces a single actual point to cover all
classes when t>=2. Otherwise choose an empty-actual pattern of owner h
with targets T, |T|<=1. Every class outside {h} union T must have ALL
patterns target h, and cap one makes these patterns empty actual with
only target h. Two such classes violate (*), so there is at most one.
Hence t<=3. If t=3, there cannot be ANY singleton-actual pattern (x,empty)
of owner h: each foreign pattern is either the same actual singleton x
or empty actual targeting h. A foreign empty pattern violates (*) with
EVERY pattern of the other foreign class. Thus both foreign classes
consist only of x, and {x,one representative of core h} is a 2-cover.
So at t=3 all patterns are empty actual, each with one target among the
other two classes (necessarily the directed 3-cycle).

LEMMA 2 (graphs). If a graph G has vertex-cover number at least three,
its edge-disjointness graph K(G) is either connected or G is K4 after
removing isolated original vertices.
Proof: if K(G) is disconnected, no component can be an isolated edge
of G, since that edge's two endpoints would cover G. Choose one
component C with disjoint edges ab,cd. Any edge outside C intersects
both, so it lies among ac,ad,bc,bd. If an edge of C uses a vertex z
outside {a,b,c,d}, it must have its other endpoint among these four;
say it is az. Then all edges outside C lie among ac,ad. If there is
only one such edge its endpoints cover G. If both exist, every edge
of C contains a or equals cd; hence {a,c} covers G. Both contradict
cover number>=3. Thus all edges of C, as well as those outside C, lie
on four vertices. Cover number>=3 then forces the complete K4.

MAIN PROOF. Suppose t>=6.
Case A: some empty-actual pattern has owner h, target set T, |T|<=2.
Discard S={h} union T, and delete target choices in S from the remaining
patterns. (Safe excision preserves intersection and gives cover number
exactly the number of remaining classes.) Every remaining pattern
originally targets h by (*), so its residual cap after excision is one.
Lemma 1 gives t<=|S|+3<=6. Equality t=6 requires |T|=2 and three
remaining classes R forming a cap-one full-Hall family. Lemma 1 says
ALL their surviving patterns have empty actual part and one R-target.
Before excision they therefore had exactly two targets, h and an
R-label, with no actual points or targets in T. Any pattern of either
class a in T must consequently target EVERY one of the three owners
in R, by (*). This contradicts cap two. Hence Case A is impossible.

Case B: every actual pattern is nonempty. Build a graph G from all
actual TWO-point patterns (these necessarily have no targets). Any two
disjoint edges of G must have the SAME owner, by (*). Thus every
nontrivial component of K(G) has one unique owner.
If tau(G)>=3 and K(G) is connected, all graph edges have one owner i.
No other class has a two-point pattern, as that would be a 2-cover of
G. Every other class's singleton-actual pattern must target i, because
no single point covers G. After excising i, the remaining family has
cap one with only actual singletons; intersection and full Hall allow
at most one class. Thus t<=2, contradiction.
If tau(G)>=3 and G=K4, its three K(G)-components are opposite-edge
pairs, each with one owner. Unless all edges have one owner (previous
case), removing the edges of ANY one owner leaves a matching pair or
a C4, neither having a one-point cover. A singleton-actual pattern of
a new owner can target at most one old owner, and its actual point
cannot hit all the remaining edges. Hence every class owns a K(G)
component, giving t<=3. Contradiction.
Therefore G has a vertex cover U of size at most two.
Restrict the whole family to members avoiding U. Its covering number
is at least t-|U|>=t-2. All remaining patterns are actual SINGLETONS,
with at most one target. Form the bipartite graph of nonempty classes
versus actual singleton values. A matching of q edges chooses q
patterns of different owners and different actual values. These q
actual petals are disjoint, so (*) needs at least binom(q,2) target
slots, while only q are available. Thus q<=3.

and actual-point vertices cover this incidence graph. Replacing each
selected class vertex by one core representative gives a cover of the
restricted full family of size at most three. Hence t-2<=3, contradiction.

labels, each core of size three, and for each class all choices of one
point from each of its two out-neighbor cores. Every member has rank
five and residual cap two. The family is intersecting and tau=5.

from itertools import combinations,product
from fractions import Fraction
from pathlib import Path
import json
n=4
pairs=list(combinations(range(n),2));actual={p:4+j for j,p in enumerate(pairs)}
stars=[set(actual[e] for e in pairs if i in e) for i in range(n)]
patterns=[];full=[]
for i in range(n):
 cl=[]
 for j in range(n):
  if j!=i:
   a=stars[i]-{actual[tuple(sorted((i,j)))]};cl.append((a,{j},False));full.append({i,j}|a)
 cl.append((stars[i],set(),True));full.append({i}|stars[i]);patterns.append(cl)
assert len({frozenset(e) for e in full})==16
assert all(len(e)==4 for e in full)
assert all(e&f for j,e in enumerate(full) for f in full[:j])
assert all(not all(set(c)&e for e in full) for c in combinations(range(10),3))
assert all(a&b for cl in patterns for a,_,_ in cl for b,_,_ in cl)
byR={};witness={}
for choices in product(range(4),repeat=4):
 chosen=[patterns[i][choices[i]] for i in range(4)]
 R=sum(seed for a,t,seed in chosen)
 Q=sum(not(a&b) for j,(a,t,s) in enumerate(chosen) for b,u,v in chosen[:j])
 if Q>byR.get(R,-1):byR[R]=Q;witness[R]=choices
# All exact positive-alpha breakpoints of possible upper-envelope lines.
points={Fraction(0)}
for r,s in combinations(byR,2):
 a=Fraction(byR[r]-byR[s],s-r)
 if a>=0:points.add(a)
points=sorted(points);checks=[]
for a in points+[points[-1]+1]:
 vals={r:Fraction(q)+a*r for r,q in byR.items()};best=max(vals.values());opt=[r for r,v in vals.items() if v==best]
 checks.append(dict(alpha=str(a),optimal_seed_counts=opt,objective=str(best)))
result=dict(t=4,k=4,n_ground=10,members=16,intersection_pairs=120,three_covers_tested=120,within_color_pairs_all_intersect=True,pure_profiles_checked=4**4,Q_max_by_seed_count=byR,exact_envelope_checks=checks)
print(json.dumps(result,indent=2))
Path('workspace/agent3_seed_bonus_pure_check.json').write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2))

from itertools import combinations
import numpy as np,scipy.optimize as opt,json
n,m=8,2;T=n*m;c=T+1;r=n-2*m
es=list(combinations(range(n),2));idx={e:j for j,e in enumerate(es)};N=len(es)
rows=[]
for a in range(n):
 star=[idx[tuple(sorted((a,b)))] for b in range(n) if b!=a]
 for h in range(m):
  i=a*m+h
  for P in combinations(star,r):
   P=set(P);omit=[b for b in range(n) if b!=a and idx[tuple(sorted((a,b)))] not in P]
   target=[b*m+j for b in omit for j in range(m)]+[T]
   row=np.zeros(N+T+1);row[list(P)]=1;row[N+i]=1
   for j in target:row[N+j]=1/c
   rows.append(row)
row=np.zeros(N+T+1);row[N+T]=1;rows.append(row)
A=np.array(rows);res=opt.linprog(np.ones(N+T+1),A_ub=-A,b_ub=-np.ones(len(rows)),bounds=(0,None),method='highs')
assert res.success
W=res.fun;x=res.x
assert np.min(A@x)>1-1e-8
positive=[i for i in range(T+1) if x[N+i]>1e-8]
assert positive==[T]
# Removing the apex class and its target incidence leaves pureactual weight .8? here16/17.
actual_mins=min(sum(x[p] for p in range(N) if row[p]) for row in rows[:-1])
assert actual_mins<1-1e-5
expected=1+(1-1/c)*N/r
assert abs(W-expected)<1e-8
assert abs(actual_mins-(1-1/c))<1e-8
out=dict(old_t=T,new_t=T+1,core_size=c,patterns=len(rows),lp_value=W,expected_value=expected,positive_core_classes=positive,remaining_actual_min_pattern_weight=actual_mins,needed_scale=c/(c-1),global_fractional_bound=2*(r+m*(2*m-1)+1)+1)
print(json.dumps(out,indent=2))
Path('workspace/agent1_fractional_core_discard_check.json').write_text(json.dumps(out,indent=2))

from itertools import combinations
from fractions import Fraction
from pathlib import Path
import json
n=8;m=2;q=2*m-1;t=n*m;r=n-2*m
edges=list(combinations(range(n),2));ind={e:j for j,e in enumerate(edges)}
stars=[set(ind[e] for e in edges if a in e) for a in range(n)]
patterns=[[set(c) for c in combinations(stars[a],r)] for a in range(n)]
checks=0
for a,b in combinations(range(n),2):
 e=ind[a,b]
 for P in patterns[a]:
  for Q in patterns[b]:
   u=e not in P;v=e not in Q
   assert (not(P&Q))==(u or v)
   assert (not(P&stars[b]))==u
   assert (not(stars[a]&Q))==v
   checks+=1
assert all(P&Q for cl in patterns for P in cl for Q in cl)
O=[{(a+j)%n for j in range(1,q+1)} for a in range(n)]
assert all(not(a in O[b] and b in O[a]) for a,b in combinations(range(n),2))
selected=[stars[a]-{ind[tuple(sorted((a,b)))] for b in O[a]} for a in range(n) for z in range(m)]
seed=[stars[a] for a in range(n) for z in range(m)]
Qold=sum(not(P&Q) for j,P in enumerate(selected) for Q in selected[:j]);assert Qold==t*m*q
# Explicit lifted realization.
N0=len(edges)
old=[{p for p in P}|{N0+i*N0+p for p in P} for i,P in enumerate(selected)]
dummy=[{N0+j*N0+p for p in A for j in range(t) if j!=i} for i,A in enumerate(seed)]
assert all(not(old[i]&dummy[i]) for i in range(t))
for i,j in combinations(range(t),2):
 assert bool(old[i]&old[j])==bool(selected[i]&selected[j])
 assert bool(old[i]&dummy[j])==bool(selected[i]&seed[j])
 assert bool(dummy[i]&old[j])==bool(seed[i]&selected[j])
 assert bool(dummy[i]&dummy[j])==bool(seed[i]&seed[j])
G=[]
for i in range(t):
 row=[]
 for j in range(t):
  if i==j:v=2
  else:v=int(bool(old[i]&old[j]))+int(bool(dummy[i]&dummy[j]))-int(bool(old[i]&dummy[j]))-int(bool(dummy[i]&old[j]))
  assert v==(2 if i==j else 0);row.append(v)
 G.append(row)
cert=[]
for alpha in (Fraction(m*q)-Fraction(1,2),Fraction(m*q),Fraction(m*q)+Fraction(1,2)):
 w=(1+m*q-alpha)/2
 cross=sum(w*w*int(not(old[i]&old[j]))+w*(1-w)*int(not(old[i]&dummy[j]))+(1-w)*w*int(not(dummy[i]&old[j]))+(1-w)**2*int(not(dummy[i]&dummy[j])) for i,j in combinations(range(t),2))
 within=t*w*(1-w);bonus=alpha*t*(1-w);value=cross+within+bonus
 upper=alpha*t+t*((m*q-alpha+1)*w-w*w)
 assert value==upper
 cert.append(dict(alpha=str(alpha),old_mass_per_color=str(w),objective=str(value),global_upper_bound=str(upper)))
res=dict(n=n,m=m,t=t,actual_rank=r,target_size=m*q,patterns_per_color=len(patterns[0]),cross_pattern_pairs_checked=checks,original_actual_Qmax=Qold,lifted_point_ground=(t+1)*N0,lifted_old_ranks=sorted(set(map(len,old))),dummy_ranks=sorted(set(map(len,dummy))),Gram='2I_%d'%t,global_mixed_optimality_certificates=cert)
print(json.dumps(res,indent=2))
Path('workspace/agent3_lifted_star_qp_checks.json').write_text(json.dumps(res,indent=2))
Path('workspace/agent3_lifted_star_qp_checks.py').write_text(Path('scratchpad.py').read_text())
Path('workspace/agent3_lifted_star_qp_proof.txt').write_text('''EXACT STAR QP OPTIMUM AND LIMITATION OF LIFTED-SEED ROOT METHOD
Parameters n>4m-1, q=2m-1, T=nm, actual rank r=n-2m. Each of m classes at center a has all r-subsets of the n-1 actual K_n star points; its seed is the whole star. Every old pattern omits exactly q neighbor centers. Let w_i be total old mass of color i, and p_i(b) its conditional probability of omitting bridge to center b.
For colors i,j at different centers a,b, the old-old petals are disjoint iff at least one side omits bridge ab. Old_i/seed_j are disjoint iff i omits b. Seeds always intersect. Thus cross-color Q contribution is w_i p_i(b)+w_j p_j(a)-w_i w_j p_i(b)p_j(a). At the same center all petals intersect, so contribution zero. Summing the linear terms over the m copies at every neighbor gives mq sum_i w_i. Therefore original actual Q is at most Tmq, attained by pure old choices with no mutual omissions.
Such omissions exist: choose an oriented q-outregular cyclic graph on centers (steps 1,...,q), possible since n>=2q+1. Let every class at center a omit exactly its q outneighbors. No two centers omit one another. This attains original Q=Tmq exactly. The Hall condition holds for these ACTUAL FAMILIES: a point set C of actual K_n edges covers every r-subset of star(a) iff deg_C(a)>=q+1=2m; the number of activated colors is m times activated centers, at most |C| by the handshake lemma. Any color subunion has no larger activation count. Thus this really tests the full-Hall colored QP scale, not a deficient example.
LIFT: old P_i contains common p and private(p,i) for every p in P_i; dummy seed i contains private(p,j) for p in seed A_i and j!=i. Old rank doubles; dummy rank is (T-1)(n-1). For T>=3 all cross-color intersections agree with original old/seed intersections, while own old/dummy are disjoint. So within-color Q is w_i(1-w_i), all old-old pairs within a color still intersect.
With bonus alpha times dummy mass, f=alpha*T+sum_i[(mq-alpha+1)w_i-w_i^2]-sum_{i<j,different centers}w_iw_j p_i(b)p_j(a). The last term is nonpositive. Choosing the no-mutual-omission graph above sets it to zero. Thus GLOBAL optimum is attained with ALL colors mixed equally at w_i=(mq-alpha+1)/2 whenever mq-1<alpha<mq+1. The mixed root Gram has diagonal2 and off-diagonal exactly mutual-omission indicators, hence is EXACTLY 2I_T at this GLOBAL optimum.
Conclusion: the lifted-seed trick repairs the vacuous norm-zero directions of unlifted linear seed bonuses, but even full mixing at a global optimum can give completely orthogonal roots. Because dummy ranks are huge, ADE root classification alone still does not control T in terms of old rank/target budget. More seed-geometry/cover-number information is necessary.
The Python checks all 34300 cross-center pattern pairs for n8,m2 (plus all within-center intersections), explicitly realizes all lifted sets, checks the Gram2I_16, and gives exact Fraction-valued global upper-bound attainment for three interior alpha values.
''')

text=r'''INTEGER COMMON-DUMMY PHASE PARAMETER

Let t color classes have real vertices corresponding to NONEMPTY actual
sets of rank at most r, and one dummy vertex each. All dummies represent
the same fresh point. Define the symmetric disjointness coefficient D:
real-real is 1 for disjoint actual sets and 0 otherwise; real-dummy is
M, dummy-dummy is 0, and all diagonals are 0. Let
 Q(x)=1/2 sum_{v,w} D(v,w)x_v x_w,
with nonnegative mass summing to 1 in each color. Assume 0<M<1/4 and x
is a global maximum. Let R be total real mass. A color is mixed if both
its real mass and dummy mass are positive; pure-real if dummy mass 0;
pure-dummy if dummy mass 1. Suppose there is at least one mixed color.

CLAIM: delta=M(2R-t) is a NONNEGATIVE INTEGER.

Proof. Put B=J-D; on the supported color-zero-sum tangent space its
Gram form is positive semidefinite, since Q is maximal and J vanishes.
For a supported mixed real vertex S and its color dummy, u=e_S-e_dummy
has squared B-norm 2M. For any two mixed real vertices S,T, the inner
product of their corresponding roots is 2M if S,T intersect, and
2M-1 if they are disjoint. Cauchy-Schwarz excludes the latter because
1-2M>2M. Therefore ALL supported mixed real sets pairwise intersect.

For two supported real atoms A,A' in ANY pure-real color, the root
v=e_A-e_A' has squared norm 0 or 2. Its inner product with u is
1[A intersects S]-1[A' intersects S], an integer in {-1,0,1}.
Cauchy-Schwarz bounds its absolute value by 2*sqrt(M)<1, so it is zero.
Thus all supported real atoms of a pure-real color have the SAME
intersection status with S, regardless of their possibly fractional
masses. Each pure-real color has total mass exactly one.

The actual real-real disjointness degree of S is consequently the
NUMBER of pure-real colors whose entire supported actual family is
disjoint from S. No mixed color contributes, and no pure-dummy color
has real mass. This is a nonnegative integer. KKT equality between S
and its supported dummy gives
 degree(S)+M(t-R)=M R,
so degree(S)=M(2R-t)=delta, proving the claim.

BALANCED-HALL COROLLARY. If the underlying intersecting core family has
t classes AND covering number t, and all actual patterns have rank<=r,
then delta=0 is impossible when t>2r. Indeed every actual alternative P
in a mixed or pure-dummy color has real disjointness degree at most
delta by KKT. If delta=0, P intersects EVERY supported real set S.
Choose one such S, |S|<=r; it covers all mixed/pure-dummy classes. Cover
each pure-real color by one point of its own core, costing p additional
points. Since delta=0 gives R=t/2 and p<=R, this yields
 t=tau<=r+p<=r+t/2, hence t<=2r.

CAUTION: delta+1 arbitrarily chosen supported REAL ATOMS do not
necessarily have total weight>delta when pure-real colors have multiple
fractional atoms. The analogous covering argument needs atom WEIGHT
strictly exceeding delta; replacing weight by atom count is unsupported.

This phase integrality and delta=0 corollary do NOT give the missing
asymptotic bound. They strengthen the common-dummy global-QP structure
beyond arbitrary first-order nearblocker models.
'''
